section.heading: STUDY OF COMMERCIAL MOTOR VEHICLE CRASH CAUSATION.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:135 STAT. 761

paragraph.heading: Commercial motor vehicle.—
paragraph.content: The term “commercial motor vehicle” has the meaning given the term in section 31132 of title 49, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Study.—
paragraph.content: The term “study” means the study carried out under subsection (b).

subsection.heading: Study.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall carry out a comprehensive study—

paragraph.content: to determine the causes of, and contributing factors to, crashes that involve a commercial motor vehicle; and

paragraph.chapeau: to identify data requirements, data collection procedures, reports, and any other measures that can be used to improve the ability of States and the Secretary—

subparagraph.content: to evaluate future crashes involving commercial motor vehicles;
to monitor crash trends and identify causes and contributing factors; and
to develop effective safety improvement policies and programs.

subsection.heading: Design.—
subsection.chapeau: The study shall be designed to yield information that can be used to help policy makers, regulators, and law enforcement identify activities and other measures that are likely to lead to reductions in—

paragraph.content: the frequency of crashes involving a commercial motor vehicle;
the severity of crashes involving a commercial motor vehicle; and
fatalities and injuries.

subsection.heading: Consultation.—
subsection.chapeau: In designing and carrying out the study, the Secretary may consult with individuals or entities with expertise on—

paragraph.content: crash causation and prevention;
commercial motor vehicles, commercial drivers, and motor carriers, including passenger carriers;
highways and noncommercial motor vehicles and drivers;
Federal and State highway and motor carrier safety programs;
research methods and statistical analysis; and
other relevant topics, as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Public Comment.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall make available for public comment information about the objectives, methodology, implementation, findings, and other aspects of the study.

subsection.heading: Reports.—
subsection.content: As soon as practicable after the date on which the study is completed, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report describing the results of the study and any legislative recommendations to facilitate reductions in the matters described in paragraphs (1) through (3) of subsection (c).

section.heading: PROMOTING WOMEN IN THE TRUCKING WORKFORCE.

subsection.heading: Findings.—
subsection.chapeau: Congress finds that—

paragraph.content: women make up 47 percent of the workforce of the United States;

paragraph.chapeau: women are significantly underrepresented in the trucking industry, holding only 24 percent of all transportation and warehousing jobs and representing only—

subparagraph.content: 6.6 percent of truck drivers;135 STAT. 762
12.5 percent of all workers in truck transportation; and
8 percent of freight firm owners;

paragraph.content: given the total number of women truck drivers, women are underrepresented in the truck-driving workforce; and
women truck drivers have been shown to be 20 percent less likely than male counterparts to be involved in a crash.

subsection.heading: Sense of Congress Regarding Women in Trucking.—
subsection.content: It is the sense of Congress that the trucking industry should explore every opportunity to encourage and support the pursuit and retention of careers in trucking by women, including through programs that support recruitment, driver training, and mentorship.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Administrator.—
paragraph.content: The term “Administrator” means the Administrator of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.

paragraph.heading: Board.—
paragraph.content: The term “Board” means the Women of Trucking Advisory Board established under subsection (d)(1).

paragraph.heading: Large trucking company.—
paragraph.content: The term “large trucking company” means a motor carrier (as defined in section 13102 of title 49, United States Code) with more than 100 power units.

paragraph.heading: Mid-sized trucking company.—
paragraph.content: The term “mid-sized trucking company” means a motor carrier (as defined in section 13102 of title 49, United States Code) with not fewer than 11 power units and not more than 100 power units.

paragraph.heading: Power unit.—
paragraph.content: The term “power unit” means a self-propelled vehicle under the jurisdiction of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.

paragraph.heading: Small trucking company.—
paragraph.content: The term “small trucking company” means a motor carrier (as defined in section 13102 of title 49, United States Code) with not fewer than 1 power unit and not more than 10 power units.

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.chapeau: To encourage women to enter the field of trucking, the Administrator shall establish and facilitate an advisory board, to be known as the “Women of Trucking Advisory Board”, to review and report on policies that—

subparagraph.content: provide education, training, mentorship, or outreach to women in the trucking industry; and
recruit, retain, or advance women in the trucking industry.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Board shall be composed of not fewer than 8 members whose backgrounds, experience, and certifications allow those members to contribute balanced points of view and diverse ideas regarding the matters described in paragraph (3)(B).

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: Not later than 270 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall appoint the members of the Board, of whom—

subclause.content: not fewer than 1 shall be a representative of large trucking companies;
not fewer than 1 shall be a representative of mid-sized trucking companies;135 STAT. 763
not fewer than 1 shall be a representative of small trucking companies;
not fewer than 1 shall be a representative of nonprofit organizations in the trucking industry;
not fewer than 1 shall be a representative of trucking business associations;
not fewer than 1 shall be a representative of independent owner-operators;
not fewer than 1 shall be a woman who is a professional truck driver; and
not fewer than 1 shall be a representative of an institution of higher education or trucking trade school.

clause.heading: Diversity.—
clause.content: A member of the Board appointed under any of subclauses (I) through (VIII) of clause (i) may not be appointed under any other subclause of that clause.

subparagraph.heading: Terms.—
subparagraph.content: Each member shall be appointed for the life of the Board.

subparagraph.heading: Compensation.—
subparagraph.content: A member of the Board shall serve without compensation.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Board shall identify—

clause.chapeau: barriers and industry trends that directly or indirectly discourage women from pursuing and retaining careers in trucking, including—

subclause.content: any particular barriers and trends that impact women minority groups;
any particular barriers and trends that impact women who live in rural, suburban, or urban areas; and
any safety risks unique to women in the trucking industry;

clause.content: ways in which the functions of trucking companies, nonprofit organizations, training and education providers, and trucking associations may be coordinated to facilitate support for women pursuing careers in trucking;
opportunities to expand existing opportunities for women in the trucking industry; and
opportunities to enhance trucking training, mentorship, education, and advancement and outreach programs that would increase the number of women in the trucking industry.

subparagraph.heading: Report.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Board shall submit to the Administrator a report containing the findings and recommendations of the Board, including recommendations that companies, associations, institutions, other organizations, or the Administrator may adopt—

clause.content: to address any industry trends identified under subparagraph (A)(i);
to coordinate the functions of trucking companies, nonprofit organizations, and trucking associations in a manner that facilitates support for women pursuing careers in trucking;135 STAT. 764

subclause.content: to take advantage of any opportunities identified under subparagraph (A)(iii); and
to create new opportunities to expand existing scholarship opportunities for women in the trucking industry; and

clause.content: to enhance trucking training, men­tor­ship, education, and outreach programs that are exclusive to women.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report describing—

clause.content: the findings and recommendations of the Board under paragraph (3)(B); and
any actions taken by the Administrator to adopt the recommendations of the Board (or an explanation of the reasons for not adopting the recommendations).

subparagraph.heading: Public availability.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Administrator shall make the report under subparagraph (A) publicly available—

clause.content: on the website of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration; and
in appropriate offices of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.

paragraph.heading: Termination.—
paragraph.content: The Board shall terminate on submission of the report to Congress under paragraph (4).

section.heading: STATE INSPECTION OF PASSENGER-CARRYING COMMERCIAL MOTOR VEHICLES.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall solicit additional comment on the advance notice of proposed rulemaking entitled “State Inspection Programs for Passenger-Carrier Vehicles” (81 Fed. Reg. 24769 (April 27, 2016)).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: After reviewing all comments received in response to the solicitation under subsection (a), if the Secretary determines that data and information exist to support moving forward with a final rulemaking action, the Secretary shall issue a final rule relating to the advance notice of proposed rulemaking described in that subsection.

paragraph.heading: Considerations.—
paragraph.content: In determining whether to issue a final rule under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall consider the impact of continuing to allow self-inspection as a means to satisfy periodic inspection requirements on the safety of passenger carrier operations.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Labor, shall establish a task force, to be known as the “Truck Leasing Task Force” (referred to in this section as the “Task Force”).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall select not more than 10 individuals to serve as members of the Task Force, including at least 1 representative from each of the following:

subparagraph.content: Labor organizations.
Motor carriers that provide lease-purchase agreements to owner-operators.
Consumer protection groups.
Members of the legal profession who specialize in consumer finance issues, including experience with lease-purchase agreements.
Owner-operators in the trucking industry with experience regarding lease-purchase agreements.
Businesses that provide or are subject to lease-purchase agreements in the trucking industry.

paragraph.heading: Compensation.—
paragraph.content: A member of the Task Force shall serve without compensation.

subsection.heading: Duties.—
subsection.chapeau: The Task Force shall examine, at a minimum—

paragraph.content: common truck leasing arrangements available to commercial motor vehicle drivers, including lease-purchase agreements;
the terms of the leasing agreements described in paragraph (1);

subparagraph.content: the existence of inequitable leasing agreements and terms in the motor carrier industry;
whether any such inequitable terms and agreements affect the frequency of maintenance performed on vehicles subject to those agreements; and
whether any such inequitable terms and agreements affect whether a vehicle is kept in a general state of good repair;

paragraph.content: specific agreements available to drayage drivers at ports relating to the Clean Truck Program or any similar program to decrease emissions from port operations;
the impact of truck leasing agreements on the net compensation of commercial motor vehicle drivers, including port drayage drivers;
whether truck leasing agreements properly incentivize the safe operation of vehicles, including driver compliance with the hours of service regulations and laws governing speed and safety generally;
resources to assist commercial motor vehicle drivers in assessing the financial impacts of leasing agreements; and

subparagraph.content: the opportunity that equitable leasing agreements provide for drivers to start or expand trucking companies; and
the history of motor carriers starting from single owner-operators.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: On completion of the examination under subsection (c), the Task Force shall submit to the Secretary, the Secretary of Labor, and the appropriate committees of Congress a report containing—

paragraph.content: the findings of the Task Force with respect to the matters described in subsection (c);

paragraph.chapeau: best practices relating to—

subparagraph.content: assisting a commercial motor vehicle driver in assessing the impacts of leasing agreements prior to entering into such an agreement;135 STAT. 766
assisting a commercial motor vehicle driver who has entered into a predatory lease agreement; and
preventing coercion and impacts on safety as described in section 31136 of title 49, United States Code; and

paragraph.content: recommendations relating to changes to laws (including regulations), as applicable, at the Federal, State, or local level to promote fair leasing agreements under which a commercial motor vehicle driver, including a short haul driver, who is a party to such an agreement is able to earn a rate commensurate with other commercial motor vehicle drivers performing similar duties.

subsection.heading: Termination.—
subsection.content: Not later than 30 days after the date on which the report under subsection (d) is submitted, the Task Force shall terminate.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Automatic emergency braking system.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “automatic emergency braking system” means a system on a commercial motor vehicle that, based on a predefined distance and closing rate with respect to an obstacle in the path of the commercial motor vehicle—

subparagraph.content: alerts the driver of the obstacle; and
if necessary to avoid or mitigate a collision with the obstacle, automatically applies the brakes of the commercial motor vehicle.

paragraph.heading: Commercial motor vehicle.—
paragraph.content: The term “commercial motor vehicle” has the meaning given the term in section 31101 of title 49, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: prescribe a motor vehicle safety standard under section 30111 of title 49, United States Code, that requires any commercial motor vehicle subject to section 571.136 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (relating to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard Number 136) (or a successor regulation) that is manufactured after the effective date of the standard prescribed under this subparagraph to be equipped with an automatic emergency braking system; and
as part of the standard under subparagraph (A), establish performance requirements for automatic emergency braking systems.

paragraph.heading: Considerations.—
paragraph.chapeau: Prior to prescribing the motor vehicle safety standard under paragraph (1)(A), the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: conduct a review of automatic emergency braking systems in use in applicable commercial motor vehicles and address any identified deficiencies with respect to those automatic emergency braking systems in the rulemaking proceeding to prescribe the standard, if practicable; and

consult with representatives of commercial motor vehicle drivers regarding the experiences of drivers with automatic emergency braking systems in use in applicable commercial motor vehicles, including any malfunctions or 135 STAT. 767 unwarranted activations of those automatic emergency braking systems.

subsection.heading: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulation.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall prescribe a regulation under section 31136 of title 49, United States Code, that requires that an automatic emergency braking system installed in a commercial motor vehicle manufactured after the effective date of the standard prescribed under subsection (b)(1)(A) that is in operation on or after that date and is subject to section 571.136 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (relating to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard Number 136) (or a successor regulation) be used at any time during which the commercial motor vehicle is in operation.

subsection.heading: Report on Automatic Emergency Braking in Other Commercial Motor Vehicles.—

paragraph.heading: Study.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall complete a study on equipping a variety of commercial motor vehicles not subject to section 571.136 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (relating to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard Number 136) (or a successor regulation) as of that date of enactment with automatic emergency braking systems to avoid or mitigate a collision with an obstacle in the path of the commercial motor vehicle, including an assessment of the feasibility, benefits, and costs associated with installing automatic emergency braking systems on a variety of newly manufactured commercial motor vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating greater than 10,001 pounds.

paragraph.heading: Independent research.—
paragraph.chapeau: If the Secretary enters into a contract with a third party to perform research relating to the study required under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall ensure that the third party does not have any financial or contractual ties to, or relationships with—

subparagraph.content: a motor carrier that transports passengers or property for compensation;
the motor carrier industry; or
an entity producing or supplying automatic emergency braking systems.

paragraph.heading: Public comment.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the date on which the study under paragraph (1) is completed, the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: issue a notice in the Federal Register containing the findings of the study; and
provide an opportunity for public comment.

paragraph.heading: Report to congress.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the conclusion of the public comment period under paragraph (3)(B), the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committees on Transportation and Infrastructure and Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives a report that includes—

subparagraph.content: the results of the study under paragraph (1);
a summary of any comments received under paragraph (3)(B); and

a determination as to whether the Secretary intends to develop performance requirements for automatic emergency braking systems for applicable commercial 135 STAT. 768 motor vehicles, including any analysis that led to that determination.

paragraph.heading: Rulemaking.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date on which the study under paragraph (1) is completed, the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: determine whether a motor vehicle safety standard relating to equipping the commercial motor vehicles described in that paragraph with automatic emergency braking systems would meet the requirements and considerations described in subsections (a) and (b) of section 30111 of title 49, United States Code; and

if the Secretary determines that a motor vehicle safety standard described in subparagraph (A) would meet the requirements and considerations described in that subparagraph, initiate a rulemaking to prescribe such a motor vehicle safety standard.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Committee.—
paragraph.content: The term “Committee” means the Advisory Committee on Underride Protection established under subsection (d)(1).

paragraph.heading: Motor carrier.—
paragraph.content: The term “motor carrier” has the meaning given the term in section 13102 of title 49, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Passenger motor vehicle.—
paragraph.content: The term “passenger motor vehicle” has the meaning given the term in section 32101 of title 49, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Underride crash.—
paragraph.content: The term “underride crash” means a crash in which a trailer or semitrailer intrudes into the passenger compartment of a passenger motor vehicle.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall promulgate such regulations as are necessary to revise sections 571.223 and 571.224 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (relating to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard Numbers 223 and 224, respectively), to require trailers and semitrailers manufactured after the date on which those regulations are promulgated to be equipped with rear impact guards that are designed to prevent passenger compartment intrusion from a trailer or semitrailer when a passenger motor vehicle traveling at 35 miles per hour makes—

clause.content: an impact in which the passenger motor vehicle impacts the center of the rear of the trailer or semitrailer;
an impact in which 50 percent of the width of the passenger motor vehicle overlaps the rear of the trailer or semitrailer; and

an impact in which 30 percent of the width of the passenger motor vehicle overlaps the rear of the trailer or semitrailer, if the Secretary determines that a revision of sections 571.223 and 571.224 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (relating to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard Numbers 223 and 224, 135 STAT. 769 respectively) to address such an impact would meet the requirements and considerations described in subsections (a) and (b) of section 30111 of title 49, United States Code.

subparagraph.heading: Effective date.—
subparagraph.content: The regulations promulgated under subparagraph (A) shall require full compliance with each Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard revised pursuant to those regulations not later than 2 years after the date on which those regulations are promulgated.

paragraph.heading: Additional research.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall conduct additional research on the design and development of rear impact guards that can—

subparagraph.content: prevent underride crashes in cases in which the passenger motor vehicle is traveling at speeds of up to 65 miles per hour; and
protect passengers in passenger motor vehicles against severe injury in crashes in which the passenger motor vehicle is traveling at speeds of up to 65 miles per hour.

paragraph.heading: Review of standards.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 5 years after the date on which the regulations under paragraph (1)(A) are promulgated, the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: review the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards revised pursuant to those regulations and any other requirements of those regulations relating to rear underride guards on trailers or semitrailers to evaluate the need for changes in response to advancements in technology; and
update those Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards and those regulations accordingly.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall promulgate such regulations as are necessary to revise the regulations relating to minimum periodic inspection standards under appendix G to subchapter B of chapter III of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations, and the regulations relating to driver vehicle inspection reports under section 396.11 of that title to include requirements relating to rear impact guards and rear end protection that are consistent with the requirements described in section 393.86 of that title.

subparagraph.heading: Considerations.—
subparagraph.content: In revising the regulations described in subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall consider it to be a defect or a deficiency if a rear impact guard is missing an, or has a corroded or compromised, element that affects the structural integrity and protective feature of the rear impact guard.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: complete additional research on side underride guards to better understand the overall effectiveness of side underride guards;

assess the feasibility, benefits, and costs of, and any impacts on intermodal equipment, freight mobility (including port operations), and freight capacity associated 135 STAT. 770 with, installing side underride guards on newly manufactured trailers and semitrailers with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 pounds or more;

subparagraph.chapeau: consider the unique structural and operational aspects of—

clause.content: intermodal chassis (as defined in section 340.2 of title 46, Code of Federal Regulations; and
pole trailers (as defined in section 390.5 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations; and

subparagraph.content: if warranted, develop performance standards for side underride guards.

paragraph.heading: Independent research.—
paragraph.chapeau: If the Secretary enters into a contract with a third party to perform the research required under paragraph (1)(A), the Secretary shall ensure that the third party does not have any financial or contractual ties to, or relationships with—

subparagraph.content: a motor carrier that transports passengers or property for compensation;
the motor carrier industry; or
an entity producing or supplying underride guards.

paragraph.heading: Publication of assessment.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after completion of the assessment required under paragraph (1)(B), the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: issue a notice in the Federal Register containing the findings of the assessment; and
provide an opportunity for public comment.

paragraph.heading: Report to congress.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the conclusion of the public comment period under paragraph (3)(B), the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report that includes—

subparagraph.content: the results of the assessment under paragraph (1)(B);
a summary of any comments received by the Secretary under paragraph (3)(B); and
a determination as to whether the Secretary intends to develop performance requirements for side underride guards, including any analysis that led to that determination.

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish an Advisory Committee on Underride Protection to provide advice and recommendations to the Secretary on safety regulations to reduce underride crashes and fatalities relating to underride crashes.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Committee shall be composed of not more than 20 members, appointed by the Secretary, who—

clause.content: are not employees of the Department; and
are qualified to serve on the Committee because of their expertise, training, or experience.

subparagraph.heading: Representation.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Committee shall include 2 representatives of each of the following:

clause.content: Truck and trailer manufacturers.135 STAT. 771
Motor carriers, including independent owner-operators.
Law enforcement.
Motor vehicle engineers.
Motor vehicle crash investigators.
Truck safety organizations.
The insurance industry.
Emergency medical service providers.
Families of underride crash victims.
Labor organizations.

paragraph.heading: Compensation.—
paragraph.content: Members of the Committee shall serve without compensation.

paragraph.heading: Meetings.—
paragraph.content: The Committee shall meet not less frequently than annually.

paragraph.heading: Support.—
paragraph.content: On request of the Committee, the Secretary shall provide information, administrative services, and supplies necessary for the Committee to carry out the duties of the Committee.

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Committee shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a biennial report that—

subparagraph.content: describes the advice and recommendations made to the Secretary; and
includes an assessment of progress made by the Secretary in advancing safety regulations relating to underride crashes.

subsection.heading: Data Collection.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall implement the recommendations described in the report of the Government Accountability Office entitled “Truck Underride Guards: Improved Data Collection, Inspections, and Research Needed”, published on March 14, 2019, and numbered GAO–19–264.

section.heading: PROVIDERS OF RECREATIONAL ACTIVITIES.
section.chapeau: Section 13506(b) of title 49, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.content: in paragraph (2), by striking “or” at the end;
in paragraph (3), by striking the period at the end and inserting “; or”; and

by adding at the end the following:“(4) transportation by a motor vehicle designed or used to transport not fewer than 9, and not more than 15, passengers (including the driver), whether operated alone or with a trailer attached for the transport of recreational equipment, if—“(A) the motor vehicle is operated by a person that provides recreational activities; “(B) the transportation is provided within a 150 air-mile radius of the location at which passengers initially boarded the motor vehicle at the outset of the trip; and “(C) in the case of a motor vehicle transporting passengers over a route between a place in a State and a place in another State, the person operating the motor vehicle is lawfully providing transportation of passengers over the entire route in accordance with applicable State law.”
.135 STAT. 772

section.heading: AMENDMENTS TO REGULATIONS RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION OF HOUSEHOLD GOODS IN INTERSTATE COMMERCE.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Administration.—
paragraph.content: The term “Administration” means the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.

paragraph.heading: Covered carrier.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “covered carrier” means a motor carrier that is—

subparagraph.content: engaged in the interstate transportation of household goods; and

subject to the requirements of part 375 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on the effective date of any amendments made pursuant to the notice of proposed rulemaking issued under subsection (b)).

subsection.heading: Amendments to Regulations.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall issue a notice of proposed rulemaking to amend, as the Secretary determines to be appropriate, regulations relating to the interstate transportation of household goods.

subsection.heading: Considerations.—
subsection.chapeau: In issuing the notice of proposed rulemaking under subsection (b), the Secretary shall consider amending the following provisions of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations, in accordance with the following recommendations:

paragraph.chapeau: Section 375.207(b) to require each covered carrier to include on the website of the covered carrier a link—

subparagraph.content: to the publication of the Administration entitled “Ready to Move–Tips for a Successful Interstate Move” and numbered ESA–03–005 on the website of the Administration; or
to a copy of the publication referred to in subparagraph (A) on the website of the covered carrier.

paragraph.content: Subsections (a) and (b)(1) of section 375.213 to require each covered carrier to provide to each individual shipper, together with any written estimate provided to the shipper, a copy of the publication described in appendix A of part 375 of that title, entitled “Your Rights and Responsibilities When You Move” and numbered ESA–03–006 (or a successor publication), in the form of a written copy or a hyperlink on the website of the covered carrier to the location on the website of the Administration containing that publication.
Section 375.213 to repeal subsection (e) of that section.

paragraph.chapeau: Section 375.401(a) to require each covered carrier—

subparagraph.chapeau: to conduct a visual survey of the household goods to be transported by the covered carrier—

clause.content: in person; or

clause.chapeau: virtually, using—

subclause.content: a remote camera; or
another appropriate technology;

subparagraph.chapeau: to offer a visual survey described in subparagraph (A) for all household goods shipments, regardless of the distance between—

clause.content: the location of the household goods; and
the location of the agent of the covered carrier preparing the estimate; and

subparagraph.content: to provide to each shipper a copy of the publication of the Administration entitled “Ready to Move–Tips for a Successful Interstate Move” and numbered ESA–03–005 135 STAT. 773 on receipt from the shipper of a request to schedule, or a waiver of, a visual survey offered under subparagraph (B).

paragraph.chapeau: Sections 375.401(b)(1), 375.403(a)(6)(ii), and 375.405(b)(7)(ii), and subpart D of appendix A of part 375, to require that, in any case in which a shipper tenders any additional item or requests any additional service prior to loading a shipment, the affected covered carrier shall—

subparagraph.content: prepare a new estimate; and
maintain a record of the date, time, and manner in which the new estimate was accepted by the shipper.

paragraph.content: Section 375.501(a), to establish that a covered carrier is not required to provide to a shipper an order for service if the covered carrier elects to provide the information described in paragraphs (1) through (15) of that section in a bill of lading that is presented to the shipper before the covered carrier receives the shipment.
Subpart H of part 375, to replace the replace the terms “freight bill” and “expense bill” with the term “invoice”.

section.heading: IMPROVING FEDERAL-STATE MOTOR CARRIER SAFETY ENFORCEMENT COORDINATION.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Covered state.—
paragraph.content: The term “covered State” means a State that receives Federal funds under the motor carrier safety assistance program established under section 31102 of title 49, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Imminent hazard.—
paragraph.content: The term “imminent hazard” has the same meaning as in section 521 of title 49, United States Code.

subsection.heading: Review and Enforcement of State Out-of-service Orders.—
subsection.content: As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register a process under which the Secretary shall review each out-of-service order issued by a covered State in accordance with section 31144(d) of title 49, United States Code, by not later than 30 days after the date on which the out-of-service order is submitted to the Secretary by the covered State.

subsection.heading: Review and Enforcement of State Imminent Hazard Determinations.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register a process under which the Secretary shall review imminent hazard determinations made by covered States.

paragraph.heading: Enforcement.—
paragraph.content: On reviewing an imminent hazard determination under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall pursue enforcement under section 521 of title 49, United States Code, as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Limousine.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “limousine” means a motor vehicle—

subparagraph.content: that has a seating capacity of 9 or more persons (including the driver);
with a gross vehicle weight rating greater than 10,000 pounds but not greater than 26,000 pounds;135 STAT. 774

subparagraph.chapeau: that the Secretary has determined by regulation has physical characteristics resembling—

clause.content: a passenger car;
a multipurpose passenger vehicle; or
a truck with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 pounds or less; and

subparagraph.content: that is not a taxi, nonemergency medical, or paratransit motor vehicle.

paragraph.heading: Limousine operator.—
paragraph.content: The term “limousine operator” means a person who owns or leases, and uses, a limousine to transport passengers for compensation.

paragraph.heading: Motor vehicle safety standard.—
paragraph.content: The term “motor vehicle safety standard” has the meaning given the term in section 30102(a) of title 49, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” has the meaning given such term in section 30102(a) of title 49, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Research.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 4 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall complete research into the development of motor vehicle safety standards for side impact protection, roof crush resistance, and air bag systems for the protection of occupants in limousines with alternative seating positions, including perimeter seating arrangements.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: Subject to clause (ii), not later than 2 years after the date on which the research under paragraph (1) is completed, the Secretary shall prescribe, for the protection of occupants in limousines with alternative seating positions, a final motor vehicle safety standard for each of the following:

subclause.content: Side impact protection.
Roof crush resistance.
Air bag systems.

clause.heading: Requirements and considerations.—
clause.content: The Secretary may only prescribe a motor vehicle safety standard described in clause (i) if the Secretary determines that the standard meets the requirements and considerations described in subsections (a) and (b) of section 30111 of title 49, United States Code.

subparagraph.heading: Report.—
subparagraph.content: If the Secretary determines that a motor vehicle safety standard described in subparagraph (A)(i) would not meet the requirements and considerations described in subsections (a) and (b) of section 30111 of title 49, United States Code, the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register and submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives a report describing the reasons for not prescribing the standard.

paragraph.heading: Research.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall complete research into safety features and standards that aid evacuation in the event that an exit in the passenger compartment of a limousine is blocked.135 STAT. 775

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Subject to clause (ii), not later than 2 years after the date on which the research under paragraph (1) is completed, the Secretary shall prescribe a final motor vehicle safety standard based on the results of that research.

clause.heading: Requirements and considerations.—
clause.content: The Secretary may only prescribe a motor vehicle safety standard described in clause (i) if the Secretary determines that the standard meets the requirements and considerations described in subsections (a) and (b) of section 30111 of title 49, United States Code.

subparagraph.heading: Report.—
subparagraph.content: If the Secretary determines that a standard described in subparagraph (A)(i) would not meet the requirements and considerations described in subsections (a) and (b) of section 30111 of title 49, United States Code, the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register and submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives a report describing the reasons for not prescribing the standard.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: A limousine operator may not introduce a limousine into interstate commerce unless the limousine operator has prominently disclosed in a clear and conspicuous notice, including on the website of the operator if the operator has a website, the following:

subparagraph.content: The date of the most recent inspection of the limousine required under State or Federal law, if applicable.
The results of the inspection, if applicable.
Any corrective action taken by the limousine operator to ensure the limousine passed inspection, if applicable.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Federal Trade Commission shall enforce this subsection in the same manner, by the same means, and with the same jurisdiction, powers, and duties as though all applicable terms and provisions of the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.) were incorporated into and made a part of this subsection.

subparagraph.heading: Treatment.—
subparagraph.content: Any person who violates this subsection shall be subject to the penalties and entitled to the privileges and immunities provided in the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Savings provision.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this subsection limits the authority of the Federal Trade Commission under any other provision of law.

paragraph.heading: Effective date.—
paragraph.content: This subsection shall take effect on the date that is 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and 135 STAT. 776 Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report on the National Consumer Complaint Database of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.

subsection.heading: Contents.—
subsection.chapeau: The report under subsection (a) shall include—

paragraph.content: a review of the process and effectiveness of efforts to review and follow-up on complaints submitted to the National Consumer Complaint Database;
an identification of the top 5 complaint categories;

paragraph.chapeau: an identification of—

subparagraph.content: the process that the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration uses to determine which entities to take enforcement actions against; and
the top categories of enforcement actions taken by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration;

paragraph.content: a review of the use of the National Consumer Complaint Database website over the 5-year period ending on December 31, 2020, including information obtained by conducting interviews with drivers, customers of movers of household goods, brokers, motor carriers, including small business motor carriers, and other users of the website to determine the usability of the website;
a review of efforts taken by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration to raise awareness of the National Consumer Complaint Database; and

paragraph.chapeau: recommendations, as appropriate, including with respect to methods—

subparagraph.content: for improving the usability of the National Consumer Complaint Database website;
for improving the review of complaints;
for using data collected through the National Consumer Complaint Database to identify bad actors;
to improve confidence and transparency in the complaint process; and

for improving stakeholder awareness of and participation in the National Consumer Complaint Database and the complaint system, including improved communication about the purpose of the National Consumer Complaint Database.

section.heading: ELECTRONIC LOGGING DEVICE OVERSIGHT.
section.chapeau: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report analyzing the cost and effectiveness of electronic logging devices and detailing the processes—

paragraph.chapeau: used by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration—

subparagraph.content: to review electronic logging device logs; and
to protect proprietary information and personally identifiable information obtained from electronic logging device logs; and

paragraph.content: through which an operator may challenge or appeal a violation notice issued by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration relating to an electronic logging device.135 STAT. 777

section.heading: TRANSPORTATION OF AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES AND FARM SUPPLIES.
section.chapeau: Section 229(a)(1) of the Motor Carrier Safety Improvement Act of 1999 (49 U.S.C. 31136 note; Public Law 106–159) is amended—

paragraph.content: in subparagraph (B), by striking “or” at the end;
in subparagraph (C), by striking the period at the end and inserting “; or”; and

by adding at the end the following:“(D) drivers transporting livestock (as defined in section 602 of the Emergency Livestock Feed Assistance Act of 1988 (7 U.S.C. 1471) including insects) within a 150 air-mile radius from the final destination of the livestock.” .

section.heading: MODIFICATION OF RESTRICTIONS ON CERTAIN COMMERCIAL DRIVER’S LICENSES.
section.content: The Administrator of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration shall revise section 383.3(f)(3)(ii) of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (or a successor regulation), to provide that a restricted commercial driver’s license issued to an employee in a farm-related service industry shall be limited to the applicable seasonal periods defined by the State issuing the restricted commercial driver’s license, subject to the condition that the total number of days in any calendar year during which the restricted commercial driver’s license is valid does not exceed 210.

section.heading: REPORT ON HUMAN TRAFFICKING VIOLATIONS INVOLVING COMMERCIAL MOTOR VEHICLES.
section.content: Not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act, and every 3 years thereafter, the Secretary, acting through the Department of Transportation Advisory Committee on Human Trafficking established under section 5(a) of the Combating Human Trafficking in Commercial Vehicles Act (Public Law 115–99; 131 Stat. 2243), shall coordinate with the Attorney General to prepare and submit to Congress a report relating to human trafficking violations involving commercial motor vehicles, which shall include recommendations for countering human trafficking, including an assessment of previous best practices by transportation stakeholders.

section.heading: BROKER GUIDANCE RELATING TO FEDERAL MOTOR CARRIER SAFETY REGULATIONS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall issue guidance to clarify the definitions of the terms “broker” and “bona fide agents” in section 371.2 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations.

subsection.heading: Considerations.—
subsection.chapeau: In issuing guidance under subsection (a), the Secretary shall take into consideration—

paragraph.content: the extent to which technology has changed the nature of freight brokerage;
the role of bona fide agents; and
other aspects of the freight transportation industry.

subsection.heading: Dispatch Services.—
subsection.chapeau: In issuing guidance under subsection (a), the Secretary shall, at a minimum—

paragraph.content: examine the role of a dispatch service in the transportation industry;
examine the extent to which dispatch services could be considered brokers or bona fide agents; and135 STAT. 778
clarify the level of financial penalties for unauthorized brokerage activities under section 14916 of title 49, United States Code, applicable to a dispatch service.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Apprentice.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “apprentice” means an individual who—

subparagraph.content: is under the age of 21; and
holds a commercial driver’s license.

paragraph.heading: Commercial driver’s license.—
paragraph.content: The term “commercial driver’s license” has the meaning given the term in section 31301 of title 49, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Commercial motor vehicle.—
paragraph.content: The term “commercial motor vehicle” has the meaning given the term in section 390.5 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on the date of enactment of this Act).

paragraph.heading: Driving time.—
paragraph.content: The term “driving time” has the meaning given the term in section 395.2 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on the date of enactment of this Act).

paragraph.heading: Experienced driver.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “experienced driver” means an individual who—

subparagraph.content: is not younger than 26 years of age;
has held a commercial driver’s license for the 2-year period ending on the date on which the individual serves as an experienced driver under subsection (b)(2)(C)(ii);

subparagraph.chapeau: during the 2-year period ending on the date on which the individual serves as an experienced driver under subsection (b)(2)(C)(ii), has had no—

clause.content: preventable accidents reportable to the Department; or
pointed moving violations; and

subparagraph.content: has a minimum of 5 years of experience driving a commercial motor vehicle in interstate commerce.

paragraph.heading: On-duty time.—
paragraph.content: The term “on-duty time” has the meaning given the term in section 395.2 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on the date of enactment of this Act).

paragraph.heading: Pointed moving violation.—
paragraph.content: The term “pointed moving violation” means a violation that results in points being added to the license of a driver, or a similar comparable violation, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall establish, in accordance with section 31315(c) of title 49, United States Code, a pilot program allowing employers to establish the apprenticeship programs described in paragraph (2).

paragraph.heading: Description of apprenticeship program.—
paragraph.chapeau: An apprenticeship program referred to in paragraph (1) is a program that consists of the following requirements:

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The apprentice shall complete 120 hours of on-duty time, of which not less than 135 STAT. 779 80 hours shall be driving time in a commercial motor vehicle.

clause.heading: Performance benchmarks.—
clause.chapeau: To complete the 120-hour probationary period under clause (i), the employer of an apprentice shall determine that the apprentice is competent in each of the following areas:

subclause.content: Interstate, city traffic, rural 2-lane, and evening driving.
Safety awareness.
Speed and space management.
Lane control.
Mirror scanning.
Right and left turns.
Logging and complying with rules relating to hours of service.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: After completing the 120-hour probationary period under subparagraph (A), an apprentice shall complete 280 hours of on-duty time, of which not less than 160 hours shall be driving time in a commercial motor vehicle.

clause.heading: Performance benchmarks.—
clause.chapeau: To complete the 280-hour probationary period under clause (i), the employer of an apprentice shall determine that the apprentice is competent in each of the following areas:

subclause.content: Backing and maneuvering in close quarters.
Pretrip inspections.
Fueling procedures.
Weighing loads, weight distribution, and sliding tandems.
Coupling and uncoupling procedures.
Trip planning, truck routes, map reading, navigation, and permits.

subparagraph.heading: Restrictions for probationary periods.—
subparagraph.chapeau: During the 120-hour probationary period under subparagraph (A) and the 280-hour probationary period under subparagraph (B)—

clause.chapeau: an apprentice may only drive a commercial motor vehicle that has—

subclause.content: an automatic manual or automatic transmission;
an active braking collision mitigation system;
a forward-facing video event capture system; and

subclause.chapeau: a governed speed of 65 miles per hour—

item.content: at the pedal; and
under adaptive cruise control; and

clause.content: an apprentice shall be accompanied in the passenger seat of the commercial motor vehicle by an experienced driver.

subparagraph.heading: Records retention.—
subparagraph.content: The employer of an apprentice shall maintain records, in a manner required by the Secretary, relating to the satisfaction of the performance benchmarks described in subparagraphs (A)(ii) and (B)(ii) by the apprentice.135 STAT. 780

subparagraph.heading: Reportable incidents.—
subparagraph.content: If an apprentice is involved in a preventable accident reportable to the Department or a pointed moving violation while driving a commercial motor vehicle as part of an apprenticeship program described in this paragraph, the apprentice shall undergo remediation and additional training until the apprentice can demonstrate, to the satisfaction of the employer, competence in each of the performance benchmarks described in subparagraphs (A)(ii) and (B)(ii).

subparagraph.heading: Completion of program.—
subparagraph.content: An apprentice shall be considered to have completed an apprenticeship program on the date on which the apprentice completes the 280-hour probationary period under subparagraph (B).

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Nothing in this section prevents an employer from imposing any additional requirement on an apprentice participating in an apprenticeship program established under this section.

clause.heading: Technologies.—
clause.content: Nothing in this section prevents an employer from requiring or installing in a commercial motor vehicle any technology in addition to the technologies described in subparagraph (C)(i).

paragraph.heading: Apprentices.—
paragraph.chapeau: An apprentice may—

subparagraph.content: drive a commercial motor vehicle in interstate commerce while participating in the 120-hour probationary period under paragraph (2)(A) or the 280-hour probationary period under paragraph (2)(B) pursuant to an apprenticeship program established by an employer in accordance with this section; and

drive a commercial motor vehicle in interstate commerce after the apprentice completes an apprenticeship program described in paragraph (2), unless the Secretary determines there exists a safety concern.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may not allow more than 3,000 apprentices at any 1 time to participate in the pilot program established under paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Termination.—
subsection.chapeau: Effective beginning on the date that is 3 years after the date of establishment of the pilot program under subsection (b)(1)—

paragraph.content: the pilot program shall terminate; and

any driver under the age of 21 who has completed an apprenticeship program described in subsection (b)(2) may drive a commercial motor vehicle in interstate commerce, unless the Secretary determines there exists a safety concern.

subsection.heading: No Effect on License Requirement.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section exempts an apprentice from any requirement to hold a commercial driver’s license in order to operate a commercial motor vehicle.

subsection.heading: Data Collection.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall collect and analyze—

paragraph.content: data relating to any incident in which an apprentice participating in the pilot program established under subsection (b)(1) is involved;
data relating to any incident in which a driver under the age of 21 operating a commercial motor vehicle in intrastate commerce is involved; and135 STAT. 781
such other data relating to the safety of apprentices aged 18 to 20 years operating in interstate commerce as the Secretary determines to be necessary.

subsection.heading: Limitation.—
subsection.chapeau: A driver under the age of 21 participating in the pilot program under this section may not—

paragraph.chapeau: transport—

subparagraph.content: a passenger; or
hazardous cargo; or

paragraph.chapeau: operate a commercial motor vehicle—

subparagraph.content: in special configuration; or
with a gross vehicle weight rating of more than 80,000 pounds.

subsection.heading: Report to Congress.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 120 days after the date of conclusion of the pilot program under subsection (b), the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report including—

paragraph.content: the findings and conclusions resulting from the pilot program, including with respect to technologies or training provided by commercial motor carriers for apprentices as part of the pilot program to successfully improve safety;
an analysis of the safety record of apprentices participating in the pilot program, as compared to other commercial motor vehicle drivers;
the number of drivers that discontinued participation in the apprenticeship program before completion;
a comparison of the safety records of participating drivers before, during, and after the probationary periods under subparagraphs (A) and (B) of subsection (b)(2);

a comparison, for each participating driver, of average on-duty time, driving time, and time spent away from home terminal before, during, and after the probationary periods referred to in paragraph (4); and

a recommendation, based on the data collected, regarding whether the level of safety achieved by the pilot program is equivalent to, or greater than, the level of safety for equivalent commercial motor vehicle drivers aged 21 years or older.

subsection.heading: Rule of Construction.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section affects the authority of the Secretary under section 31315 of title 49, United States Code, with respect to the pilot program established under subsection (b)(1), including the authority to revoke participation in, and terminate, the pilot program under paragraphs (3) and (4) of subsection (c) of that section.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, acting through the Administrator of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration, shall offer to enter into a contract with the Transportation Research Board under which the Transportation Research Board shall conduct a study of the impacts of various methods of driver compensation on safety and driver retention, including—

subparagraph.content: hourly pay;
payment for detention time; and
other payment methods used in the industry as of the date on which the study is conducted.135 STAT. 782

paragraph.heading: Consultation.—
paragraph.chapeau: In conducting the study under paragraph (1), the Transportation Research Board shall consult with—

subparagraph.content: labor organizations representing commercial motor vehicle drivers;
representatives of the motor carrier industry, including owner-operators; and
such other stakeholders as the Transportation Research Board determines to be relevant.

section.heading: LIMOUSINE COMPLIANCE WITH FEDERAL SAFETY STANDARDS.

paragraph.heading: Safety belt and seating system standards for limousines.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall prescribe a final rule that—

subparagraph.chapeau: amends Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard Numbers 208, 209, and 210 to require to be installed in limousines on each designated seating position, including on side-facing seats—

clause.content: an occupant restraint system consisting of integrated lap-shoulder belts; or
an occupant restraint system consisting of a lap belt, if an occupant restraint system described in clause (i) does not meet the need for motor vehicle safety; and

subparagraph.content: amends Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard Number 207 to require limousines to meet standards for seats (including side-facing seats), seat attachment assemblies, and seat installation to minimize the possibility of failure by forces acting on the seats, attachment assemblies, and installations as a result of motor vehicle impact.

paragraph.heading: Report on retrofit assessment for limousines.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives a report that assesses the feasibility, benefits, and costs with respect to the application of any requirement established under paragraph (1) to a limousine introduced into interstate commerce before the date on which the requirement takes effect.

subsection.heading: Modifications of Certain Vehicles.—
subsection.content: The final rule prescribed under subsection (a)(1) and any standards prescribed under subsection (b) or (c) of section 23015 shall apply to a person modifying a passenger motor vehicle (as defined in section 32101 of title 49, United States Code) that has already been purchased by the first purchaser (as defined in section 30102(b) of that title) by increasing the wheelbase of the vehicle to make the vehicle a limousine.

subsection.heading: Application.—
subsection.content: The requirements of this section apply notwithstanding section 30112(b)(1) of title 49, United States Code.135 STAT. 783

“§ 406.
23 USC 406. General requirements for Federal assistance“(a) Definition of Funded Project.—In this section, the term ‘funded project’ means a project funded, in whole or in part, by a grant provided under section 402 or 405. “(b) Regulatory Authority.—Each funded project shall be carried out in accordance with applicable regulations promulgated by the Secretary. “(c) State Matching Requirements.—If a grant provided under this chapter requires any State to share in the cost of a funded project, the aggregate of the expenditures made by the State (including any political subdivision of the State) for highway safety activities during a fiscal year, exclusive of Federal funds, for carrying out the funded project (other than expenditures for planning or administration) shall be credited toward the non-Federal share of the cost of any other funded project (other than planning and administration) during that fiscal year, regardless of whether those expenditures were made in connection with the project. “(d) Grant Application and Deadline.—“(1) Applications.—To be eligible to receive a grant under this chapter, a State shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require. “(2) Deadline.—The Secretary shall establish a single deadline for the submission of applications under paragraph (1) to enable the provision of grants under this chapter early in each applicable fiscal year beginning after the date of submission.

Deadline.Distribution of Funds to States.—Not later than 60 days after the later of the start of a fiscal year or the date of enactment of any appropriations Act making funds available to carry out this chapter for that fiscal year, the Secretary shall distribute to each State the portion of those funds to which the State is entitled for the applicable fiscal year.”

“(2) State highway safety plan website.—“(A) In general.—In carrying out paragraph (1), the Secretary shall establish a public website that is easily accessible, navigable, and searchable for the information required under that paragraph, in order to foster greater transparency in approved State highway safety programs.
“(B) Contents.—The website established under subparagraph (A) shall—“(i) include the applicable triennial highway safety plan, and the annual report, of each State submitted to, and approved by, the Secretary under subsection (k); and
“(ii) provide a means for the public to search the website for State highway safety program content required under subsection (k), including—“(I) performance measures required by the Secretary;
“(II) progress made toward meeting the applicable performance targets during the preceding program year;
“(III) program areas and expenditures; and
“(IV) a description of any sources of funds, other than funds provided under this section, that the State proposes to use to carry out the triennial highway safety plan of the State.”

section.heading: HIGHWAY SAFETY RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT.
section.chapeau: Section 403 of title 23, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.content: by striking “accident” each place it appears and inserting “crash”;

by redesignating paragraphs (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5) as paragraphs (2), (3), (4), (5), and (1), respectively, and moving the paragraphs so as to appear in numerical order; and

paragraph.content:
by adding at the end the following:“(k) Child Safety Campaign.—“(1) In general.—The Secretary shall carry out an education campaign to reduce the incidence of vehicular heatstroke of children left in passenger motor vehicles (as defined in section 30102(a) of title 49). “(2) Advertising.—The Secretary may use, or authorize the use of, funds made available to carry out this section to pay for the development, production, and use of broadcast and print media advertising and Internet-based outreach for the education campaign under paragraph (1). “(3) Coordination.—In carrying out the education campaign under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall coordinate with—“(A) interested State and local governments; “(B) private industry; and “(C) other parties, as determined by the Secretary.
“(l) Development of State Processes for Informing Consumers of Recalls.—“(1) Definitions.—In this subsection:“(A) Motor vehicle.—The term ‘motor vehicle’ has the meaning given the term in section 30102(a) of title 49. “(B) Open recall.—The term ‘open recall’ means a motor vehicle recall—“(i) for which a notification by a manufacturer has been provided under section 30119 of title 49; and “(ii) that has not been remedied under section 30120 of that title.
“(C) Program.—The term ‘program’ means the program established under paragraph (2)(A). “(D) Registration.—The term ‘registration’ means the process for registering a motor vehicle in a State (including registration renewal). “(E) State.—The term ‘State’ has the meaning given the term in section 101(a).
“(2) Grants.—“(A)
Deadline.Establishment of program.—Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this subsection, the Secretary shall establish a program under which the Secretary shall provide grants to States for use in developing and implementing State processes for informing each applicable owner and lessee of a motor vehicle of any open recall on the motor vehicle at the time of registration of the motor vehicle in the State, in accordance with this paragraph. “(B) Eligibility.—To be eligible to receive a grant under the program, a State shall—“(i) submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require; and “(ii) agree—135 STAT. 794 “(I)
Notification.to notify each owner or lessee of a motor vehicle presented for registration in the State of any open recall on that motor vehicle; and “(II) to provide to each owner or lessee of a motor vehicle presented for registration, at no cost—
“(aa) the open recall information for the motor vehicle; and
“(bb) such other information as the Secretary may require.
“(C) Factors for consideration.—In selecting grant recipients under the program, the Secretary shall take into consideration the methodology of a State for—“(i) identifying open recalls on a motor vehicle; “(ii) informing each owner and lessee of a motor vehicle of an open recall; and “(iii) measuring performance in—“(I) informing owners and lessees of open recalls; and “(II) remedying open recalls.
“(D) Performance period.—A grant provided under the program shall require a performance period of 2 years. “(E)
Evaluation.Report.—Not later than 90 days after the date of completion of the performance period under subparagraph (D), each State that receives a grant under the program shall submit to the Secretary a report that contains such information as the Secretary considers to be necessary to evaluate the extent to which open recalls have been remedied in the State. “(F) No regulations required.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary shall not be required to issue any regulations to carry out the program.
“(3) Paperwork reduction act.—Chapter 35 of title 44 (commonly known as the ‘Paperwork Reduction Act’) shall not apply to information collected under the program. “(4) Funding.—“(A)
Time period.In general.—For each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026, the Secretary shall obligate from funds made available to carry out this section $1,500,000 to carry out the program. “(B) Reallocation.—To ensure, to the maximum extent practicable, that all amounts described in subparagraph (A) are obligated each fiscal year, the Secretary, before the last day of any fiscal year, may reallocate any of those amounts remaining available to increase the amounts made available to carry out any other activities authorized under this section.
“(m) Innovative Highway Safety Countermeasures.—“(1)
Evaluation.In general.—In conducting research under this section, the Secretary shall evaluate the effectiveness of innovative behavioral traffic safety countermeasures, other than traffic enforcement, that are considered promising or likely to be effective for the purpose of enriching revisions to the document entitled ‘Countermeasures That Work: A Highway Safety Countermeasure Guide for State Highway Safety Offices, Ninth Edition’ and numbered DOT HS 812 478 (or any successor document).135 STAT. 795 “(2) Treatment.—The research described in paragraph (1) shall be in addition to any other research carried out under this section.”
.
