subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Certified nuclear reactor.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “certified nuclear reactor” means a nuclear reactor that—

subparagraph.content: competes in a competitive electricity market; and
is certified under subsection (c)(2)(A)(i) to submit a sealed bid in accordance with subsection (d).

paragraph.heading: Credit.—
paragraph.content: The term “credit” means a credit allocated to a certified nuclear reactor under subsection (e)(2).

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish a civil nuclear credit program—

paragraph.content: to evaluate nuclear reactors that are projected to cease operations due to economic factors; and
to allocate credits to certified nuclear reactors that are selected under paragraph (1)(B) of subsection (e) to receive credits under paragraph (2) of that subsection.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In order to be certified under paragraph (2)(A)(i), the owner or operator of a nuclear reactor that is projected to cease operations due to economic factors shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary determines to be appropriate, including—

clause.chapeau: information on the operating costs necessary to make the determination described in paragraph (2)(A)(ii)(I), including—

subclause.content: the average projected annual operating loss in dollars per megawatt-hour, inclusive of the cost of operational and market risks, expected to be incurred by the nuclear reactor over the 4-year period for which credits would be allocated;135 STAT. 1020
any private or publicly available data with respect to current or projected bulk power market prices;
out-of-market revenue streams;
operations and maintenance costs;
capital costs, including fuel; and
operational and market risks;

clause.content: an estimate of the potential incremental air pollutants that would result if the nuclear reactor were to cease operations;

known information on the source of produced uranium and the location where the uranium is converted, enriched, and fabricated into fuel assemblies for the nuclear reactor for the 4-year period for which credits would be allocated; and

clause.chapeau: a detailed plan to sustain operations at the conclusion of the applicable 4-year period for which credits would be allocated—

subclause.content: without receiving additional credits; or
with the receipt of additional credits of a lower amount than the credits allocated during that 4-year credit period.

subparagraph.heading: Timeline.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall accept applications described in subparagraph (A)—

clause.content: until the date that is 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act; and
not less frequently than every year thereafter.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The owner or operator of a nuclear reactor that receives a payment from a State zero-emission credit, a State clean energy contract, or any other State program with respect to that nuclear reactor shall be eligible to submit an application under subparagraph (A) with respect to that nuclear reactor during any application period beginning after the 120-day period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act.

clause.heading: Requirement.—
clause.content: An application submitted by an owner or operator described in clause (i) with respect to a nuclear reactor described in that clause shall include all projected payments from State programs in determining the average projected annual operating loss described in subparagraph (A)(i)(I), unless the credits allocated to the nuclear reactor pursuant to that application will be used to reduce those payments.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Not later than 60 days after the applicable date under subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1), the Secretary shall determine whether to certify, in accordance with clauses (ii) and (iii), each nuclear reactor for which an application is submitted under subparagraph (A) of that paragraph.

clause.heading: Minimum requirements.—
clause.chapeau: To the maximum extent practicable, the Secretary shall only certify a nuclear reactor under clause (i) if—135 STAT. 1021

subclause.content: after considering the information submitted under paragraph (1)(A)(i), the Secretary determines that the nuclear reactor is projected to cease operations due to economic factors;

after considering the estimate submitted under paragraph (1)(A)(ii), the Secretary determines that pollutants would increase if the nuclear reactor were to cease operations and be replaced with other types of power generation; and

subclause.chapeau: the Nuclear Regulatory Commission has reasonable assurance that the nuclear reactor—

item.content: will continue to be operated in accordance with the current licensing basis (as defined in section 54.3 of title 10, Code of Federal Regulations (or successor regulations) of the nuclear reactor; and
poses no significant safety hazards.

clause.heading: Priority.—
clause.content: In determining whether to certify a nuclear reactor under clause (i), the Secretary shall give priority to a nuclear reactor that uses, to the maximum extent available, uranium that is produced, converted, enriched, and fabricated into fuel assemblies in the United States.

subparagraph.heading: Notice.—
subparagraph.chapeau: For each application received under paragraph (1)(A), the Secretary shall provide to the applicable owner or operator, as applicable—

clause.content: a notice of the certification of the applicable nuclear reactor; or
a notice that describes the reasons why the certification of the applicable nuclear reactor was denied.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Subject to paragraph (2), the Secretary shall establish a deadline by which each certified nuclear reactor shall submit to the Secretary a sealed bid that—

subparagraph.content: describes the price per megawatt-hour of the credits desired by the certified nuclear reactor, which shall not exceed the average projected annual operating loss described in subsection (c)(1)(A)(i)(I); and
includes a commitment, subject to the receipt of credits, to provide a specific number of megawatt-hours of generation during the 4-year period for which credits would be allocated.

paragraph.heading: Requirement.—
paragraph.content: The deadline established under paragraph (1) shall be not later than 30 days after the first date on which the Secretary has made the determination described in paragraph (2)(A)(i) of subsection (c) with respect to each application submitted under paragraph (1)(A) of that subsection.

paragraph.heading: Auction.—
paragraph.chapeau: Notwithstanding section 169 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2209), the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: in consultation with the heads of applicable Federal agencies, establish a process for evaluating bids submitted under subsection (d)(1) through an auction process; and
select certified nuclear reactors to be allocated credits.135 STAT. 1022

paragraph.heading: Credits.—
paragraph.content: Subject to subsection (f)(2), on selection under paragraph (1), a certified nuclear reactor shall be allocated credits for a 4-year period beginning on the date of the selection.

paragraph.heading: Requirement.—
paragraph.content: To the maximum extent practicable, the Secretary shall use the amounts made available for credits under this section to allocate credits to as many certified nuclear reactors as possible.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The owner or operator of a certified nuclear reactor may seek to recertify the nuclear reactor in accordance with this section.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.content: Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, the Secretary may not allocate any credits after September 30, 2031.

paragraph.heading: Audit.—
paragraph.content: During the 4-year period beginning on the date on which a certified nuclear reactor first receives a credit, the Secretary shall periodically audit the certified nuclear reactor.

paragraph.heading: Recapture.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall, by regulation, provide for the recapture of the allocation of any credit to a certified nuclear reactor that, during the period described in paragraph (1)—

subparagraph.content: terminates operations; or
does not operate at an annual loss in the absence of an allocation of credits to the certified nuclear reactor.

paragraph.heading: Confidentiality.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish procedures to ensure that any confidential, private, proprietary, or privileged information that is included in a sealed bid submitted under this section is not publicly disclosed or otherwise improperly used.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than January 1, 2024, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to Congress a report with respect to the credits allocated to certified nuclear reactors, which shall include—

paragraph.content: an evaluation of the effectiveness of the credits in avoiding air pollutants while ensuring grid reliability;
a quantification of the ratepayer savings achieved under this section; and
any recommendations to renew or expand the credits.

section.heading: LIMITATIONS ON ISSUANCE OF CERTAIN LEASES OF POWER PRIVILEGE.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Commission.—
paragraph.content: The term “Commission” means the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

paragraph.heading: Director.—
paragraph.content: The term “Director” means the Director of the Office of Hearings and Appeals.

paragraph.heading: Office of hearings and appeals.—
paragraph.content: The term “Office of Hearings and Appeals” means the Office of Hearings and Appeals of the Department of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: Party.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “party”, with respect to a study plan agreement, means each of the following parties to the study plan agreement:

subparagraph.content: The proposed lessee.
The Tribes.

paragraph.heading: Project.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “project” means a proposed pumped storage facility that—

subparagraph.content: would use multiple Bureau of Reclamation reservoirs; and
as of June 1, 2017, was subject to a preliminary permit issued by the Commission pursuant to section 4(f) of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 797(f)).

paragraph.heading: Proposed lessee.—
paragraph.content: The term “proposed lessee” means the proposed lessee of a project.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: Study plan.—
paragraph.content: The term “study plan” means the plan described in subsection (d)(1).

paragraph.heading: Study plan agreement.—
paragraph.content: The term “study plan agreement” means an agreement entered into under subsection (b)(1) and described in subsection (c).

paragraph.heading: Tribes.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “Tribes” means—

subparagraph.content: the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation; and
the Spokane Tribe of Indians of the Spokane Reservation.

subsection.heading: Requirement for Issuance of Leases of Power Privilege.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall not issue a lease of power privilege pursuant to section 9(c)(1) of the Reclamation Project Act of 1939 (43 U.S.C. 485h(c)(1)) (as amended by section 40335) for a project unless—

paragraph.content: the proposed lessee and the Tribes have entered into a study plan agreement; or

paragraph.chapeau: the Secretary or the Director, as applicable, makes a final determination for—

subparagraph.content: a study plan agreement under subsection (c)(2); or135 STAT. 1027
a study plan under subsection (d).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: A study plan agreement shall—

subparagraph.content: establish the deadlines for the proposed lessee to formally respond in writing to comments and study requests about the project previously submitted to the Commission;

allow for the parties to submit additional comments and study requests if any aspect of the project, as proposed, differs from an aspect of the project, as described in a preapplication document provided to the Commission;

subparagraph.chapeau: except as expressly agreed to by the parties or as provided in paragraph (2) or subsection (d), require that the proposed lessee conduct each study described in—

clause.content: a study request about the project previously submitted to the Commission; or
any additional study request submitted in accordance with the study plan agreement;

subparagraph.chapeau: require that the proposed lessee study any potential adverse economic effects of the project on the Tribes, including effects on—

clause.content: annual payments to the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation under section 5(b) of the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation Grand Coulee Dam Settlement Act (Public Law 103–436; 108 Stat. 4579); and

annual payments to the Spokane Tribe of Indians of the Spokane Reservation authorized after the date of enactment of this Act, the amount of which derives from the annual payments described in clause (i);

subparagraph.content: establish a protocol for communication and consultation between the parties;
provide mechanisms for resolving disputes between the parties regarding implementation and enforcement of the study plan agreement; and
contain other provisions determined to be appropriate by the parties.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: If the parties cannot agree to the terms of a study plan agreement or implementation of those terms, the parties shall submit to the Director, for final determination on the terms or implementation of the study plan agreement, notice of the dispute, consistent with paragraph (1)(F), to the extent the parties have agreed to a study plan agreement.

subparagraph.heading: Inclusion.—
subparagraph.content: A dispute covered by subparagraph (A) may include the view of a proposed lessee that an additional study request submitted in accordance with paragraph (1)(B) is not reasonably calculated to assist the Secretary in evaluating the potential impacts of the project.

subparagraph.heading: Timing.—
subparagraph.content: The Director shall issue a determination regarding a dispute under subparagraph (A) not later than 120 days after the date on which the Director receives notice of the dispute under that subparagraph.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The proposed lessee shall submit to the Secretary for approval a study plan that details the proposed methodology for performing each of the studies—

subparagraph.content: identified in the study plan agreement of the proposed lessee; or
determined by the Director in a final determination regarding a dispute under subsection (c)(2).

paragraph.heading: Initial determination.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 60 days after the date on which the Secretary receives the study plan under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall make an initial determination that—

subparagraph.content: approves the study plan;

subparagraph.chapeau: rejects the study plan on the grounds that the study plan—

clause.content: lacks sufficient detail on a proposed methodology for a study identified in the study plan agreement; or
is inconsistent with the study plan agreement; or

subparagraph.chapeau: imposes additional study plan requirements that the Secretary determines are necessary to adequately define the potential effects of the project on—

clause.content: the exercise of the paramount hunting, fishing, and boating rights of the Tribes reserved pursuant to the Act of June 29, 1940 (54 Stat. 703, chapter 460; 16 U.S.C. 835d et seq.);
the annual payments described in clauses (i) and (ii) of subsection (c)(1)(D);
the Columbia Basin project (as defined in section 1 of the Act of May 27, 1937 (50 Stat. 208, chapter 269; 57 Stat. 14, chapter 14; 16 U.S.C. 835));
historic properties and cultural or spiritually significant resources; and
the environment.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 30 days after the date on which the Secretary makes an initial determination under paragraph (2), the Tribes or the proposed lessee may submit to the Director an objection to the initial determination.

subparagraph.heading: Final determination.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 120 days after the date on which the Director receives an objection under subparagraph (A), the Director shall—

clause.content: hold a hearing on the record regarding the objection; and
make a final determination that establishes the study plan, including a description of studies the proposed lessee is required to perform.

paragraph.heading: No objections.—
paragraph.content: If no objections are submitted by the deadline described in paragraph (3)(A), the initial determination of the Secretary under paragraph (2) shall be final.

paragraph.heading: Consistency with rights of tribes; protection, mitigation, and enhancement of fish and wildlife.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Any lease of power privilege issued by the Secretary for a project under subsection (b) shall contain conditions—135 STAT. 1029

clause.content: to ensure that the project is consistent with, and will not interfere with, the exercise of the paramount hunting, fishing, and boating rights of the Tribes reserved pursuant to the Act of June 29, 1940 (54 Stat. 703, chapter 460; 16 U.S.C. 835d et seq.); and

to adequately and equitably protect, mitigate damages to, and enhance fish and wildlife, including related spawning grounds and habitat, affected by the development, operation, and management of the project.

subparagraph.heading: Recommendations of the tribes.—
subparagraph.content: The conditions required under subparagraph (A) shall be based on joint recommendations of the Tribes.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: If the Secretary determines that any recommendation of the Tribes under subparagraph (B) is not reasonably calculated to ensure the project is consistent with subparagraph (A) or is inconsistent with the requirements of the Reclamation Project Act of 1939 (43 U.S.C. 485 et seq.), the Secretary shall attempt to resolve any such inconsistency with the Tribes, giving due weight to the recommendations and expertise of the Tribes.

clause.heading: Publication of findings.—
clause.chapeau: If, after an attempt to resolve an inconsistency under clause (i), the Secretary does not adopt in whole or in part a recommendation of the Tribes under subparagraph (B), the Secretary shall issue each of the following findings, including a statement of the basis for each of the findings:

subclause.content: A finding that adoption of the recommendation is inconsistent with the requirements of the Reclamation Project Act of 1939 (43 U.S.C. 485 et seq.).

A finding that the conditions selected by the Secretary to be contained in the lease of power privilege under subparagraph (A) comply with the requirements of clauses (i) and (ii) of that subparagraph.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), any lease of power privilege issued by the Secretary for a project under subsection (b) shall contain conditions that require the lessee of the project to make direct payments to the Tribes through reasonable annual charges in an amount that recompenses the Tribes for any adverse economic effect of the project identified in a study performed pursuant to the study plan agreement for the project.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The amount of the annual charges described in subparagraph (A) shall be established through agreement between the proposed lessee and the Tribes.

clause.heading: Condition.—
clause.content: The agreement under clause (i), including any modification of the agreement, shall be deemed to be a condition to the lease of power privilege 135 STAT. 1030 issued by the Secretary for a project under subsection (b).

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: If the proposed lessee and the Tribes cannot agree to the terms of an agreement under subparagraph (B)(i), the proposed lessee and the Tribes shall submit notice of the dispute to the Director.

clause.heading: Resolution.—
clause.content: The Director shall resolve the dispute described in clause (i) not later than 180 days after the date on which the Director receives notice of the dispute under that clause.

paragraph.heading: Additional conditions.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may include in any lease of power privilege issued by the Secretary for a project under subsection (b) other conditions determined appropriate by the Secretary, on the condition that the conditions shall be consistent with the Reclamation Project Act of 1939 (43 U.S.C. 485 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Consultation.—
paragraph.content: In establishing conditions under this subsection, the Secretary shall consult with the Tribes.

subsection.heading: Deadlines.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary or any officer of the Office of Hearing and Appeals before whom a proceeding is pending under this section may extend any deadline or enlarge any timeframe described in this section—

paragraph.content: at the discretion of the Secretary or the officer; or
on a showing of good cause by any party.

subsection.heading: Judicial Review.—
subsection.content: Any final action of the Secretary or the Director made pursuant to this section shall be subject to judicial review in accordance with chapter 7 of title 5, United States Code.

subsection.heading: Effect on Other Projects.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section establishes any precedent or is binding on any Bureau of Reclamation lease of power privilege, other than for a project.

section.heading: CLEAN ENERGY DEMONSTRATION PROGRAM ON CURRENT AND FORMER MINE LAND.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Clean energy project.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “clean energy project” means a project that demonstrates 1 or more of the following technologies:

subparagraph.content: Solar.
Micro-grids.
Geothermal.
Direct air capture.
Fossil-fueled electricity generation with carbon capture, utilization, and sequestration.
Energy storage, including pumped storage hydropower and compressed air storage.
Advanced nuclear technologies.

paragraph.heading: Economically distressed area.—
paragraph.content: The term “economically distressed area” means an area described in section 301(a) of the Public Works and Economic Development Act of 1965 (42 U.S.C. 3161(a)).

paragraph.heading: Mine land.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “mine land” means—

subparagraph.content: land subject to titles IV and V of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 (30 U.S.C. 1231 et seq.; 30 U.S.C. 1251 et seq.); and
land that has been claimed or patented subject to sections 2319 through 2344 of the Revised Statutes (commonly known as the “Mining Law of 1872”) (30 U.S.C. 22 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Program.—
paragraph.content: The term “program” means the demonstration program established under subsection (b).

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a program to demonstrate the technical and economic viability of carrying out clean energy projects on current and former mine land.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: In carrying out the program, the Secretary shall select not more than 5 clean energy projects, to be carried out in geographically diverse regions, at least 2 of which shall be solar projects.

paragraph.heading: Eligibility.—
paragraph.content: To be eligible to be selected for participation in the program under paragraph (1), a clean energy project shall demonstrate, as determined by the Secretary, a technology on a current or former mine land site with a reasonable expectation of commercial viability.

paragraph.heading: Priority.—
paragraph.chapeau: In selecting clean energy projects for participation in the program under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall prioritize clean energy projects that will—135 STAT. 1032

subparagraph.content: be carried out in a location where the greatest number of jobs can be created from the successful demonstration of the clean energy project;
provide the greatest net impact in avoiding or reducing greenhouse gas emissions;
provide the greatest domestic job creation (both directly and indirectly) during the implementation of the clean energy project;

subparagraph.chapeau: provide the greatest job creation and economic development in the vicinity of the clean energy project, particularly—

clause.content: in economically distressed areas; and
with respect to dislocated workers who were previously employed in manufacturing, coal power plants, or coal mining;

subparagraph.content: have the greatest potential for technological innovation and commercial deployment;
have the lowest levelized cost of generated or stored energy;
have the lowest rate of greenhouse gas emissions per unit of electricity generated or stored; and
have the shortest project time from permitting to completion.

paragraph.heading: Project selection.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall solicit proposals for clean energy projects and select clean energy project finalists in consultation with the Secretary of the Interior, the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, and the Secretary of Labor.

paragraph.heading: Compatibility with existing operations.—
paragraph.chapeau: Prior to selecting a clean energy project for participation in the program under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall consult with, as applicable, mining claimholders or operators or the relevant Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement Abandoned Mine Land program office to confirm—

subparagraph.content: that the proposed project is compatible with any current mining, exploration, or reclamation activities; and
the valid existing rights of any mining claimholders or operators.

subsection.heading: Consultation.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall consult with the Director of the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, acting through the Office of Brownfields and Land Revitalization, to determine whether it is necessary to promulgate regulations or issue guidance in order to prioritize and expedite the siting of clean energy projects on current and former mine land sites.

subsection.heading: Technical Assistance.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall provide technical assistance to project applicants selected for participation in the program under subsection (c) to assess the needed interconnection, transmission, and other grid components and permitting and siting necessary to interconnect, on current and former mine land where the project will be sited, any generation or storage with the electric grid.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $500,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2022 through 2026.135 STAT. 1033

section.heading: DEFINITIONS.
section.chapeau: In this subtitle:

paragraph.heading: Administrator.—
paragraph.content: The term “Administrator” means the Administrator of the Energy Information Administration.

paragraph.heading: Annual critical minerals outlook.—
paragraph.content: The term “Annual Critical Minerals Outlook” means the Annual Critical Minerals Outlook prepared under section 7002(j)(1)(B) of the Energy Act of 2020 (30 U.S.C. 1606(j)(1)(B)).

paragraph.heading: Critical mineral.—
paragraph.content: The term “critical mineral” has the meaning given the term in section 7002(a) of the Energy Act of 2020 (30 U.S.C. 1606(a)).

paragraph.heading: Household energy burden.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “household energy burden” means the quotient obtained by dividing—

subparagraph.content: the residential energy expenditures (as defined in section 440.3 of title 10, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on the date of enactment of this Act)) of the applicable household; by
the annual income of that household.

paragraph.heading: Household with a high energy burden.—
paragraph.content: The term “household with a high energy burden” has the meaning given the term in section 440.3 of title 10, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on the date of enactment of this Act).

paragraph.heading: Large manufacturing facility.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “large manufacturing facility” means a manufacturing facility that—

subparagraph.content: annually consumes more than 35,000 megawatt-hours of electricity; or
has a peak power demand of more than 10 megawatts.

paragraph.heading: Load-serving entity.—
paragraph.content: The term “load-serving entity” has the meaning given the term in section 217(a) of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 824q(a)).

paragraph.heading: Miscellaneous electric load.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “miscellaneous electric load” means electricity that—

subparagraph.chapeau: is used by an appliance or device—

clause.content: within a building; or
to serve a building; and

subparagraph.content: is not used for heating, ventilation, air conditioning, lighting, water heating, or refrigeration.

paragraph.heading: Regional transmission organization.—
paragraph.content: The term “Regional Transmission Organization” has the meaning given 135 STAT. 1039 the term in section 3 of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 796).

paragraph.heading: Rural area.—
paragraph.content: The term “rural area” has the meaning given the term in section 609(a) of the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 (7 U.S.C. 918c(a)).

section.heading: DATA COLLECTION IN THE ELECTRICITY SECTOR.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall establish an online database to track the operation of the bulk power system in the contiguous 48 States (referred to in this section as the “Dashboard”).

subparagraph.heading: Improvement of existing dashboard.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Dashboard may be established through the improvement, in accordance with this subsection, of an existing dashboard of the Energy Information Administration, such as—

clause.content: the U.S. Electric System Operating Data dashboard; or
the Hourly Electric Grid Monitor.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall expand the Dashboard to include, to the maximum extent practicable, hourly operating data collected from the electricity balancing authorities that operate the bulk power system in all of the several States, each territory of the United States, and the District of Columbia.

subparagraph.heading: Types of data.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The hourly operating data collected under subparagraph (A) may include data relating to—

clause.content: total electricity demand;
electricity demand by subregion;
short-term electricity demand forecasts;
total electricity generation;
net electricity generation by fuel type, including renewables;
electricity stored and discharged;
total net electricity interchange;
electricity interchange with directly interconnected balancing authorities; and

clause.chapeau: where available, the estimated marginal greenhouse gas emissions per megawatt hour of electricity generated—

subclause.content: within the metered boundaries of each balancing authority; and
for each pricing node.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall establish, in accordance with section 40419 and this subsection and to the extent the Administrator determines to be appropriate, a system to harmonize the operating data on electricity generation collected under subsection (a) with—

subparagraph.content: measurements of greenhouse gas and other pollutant emissions collected by the Environmental Protection Agency;
other data collected by the Environmental Protection Agency or other relevant Federal agencies, as the Administrator determines to be appropriate; and
data collected by State or regional energy credit registries.

paragraph.heading: Outcomes.—
paragraph.chapeau: The system established under paragraph (1) shall result in an integrated dataset that includes, for any given time—

subparagraph.content: the net generation of electricity by megawatt hour within the metered boundaries of each balancing authority; and
where available, the average and marginal greenhouse gas emissions by megawatt hour of electricity generated within the metered boundaries of each balancing authority.

paragraph.heading: Real-time data dissemination.—
paragraph.chapeau: To the maximum extent practicable, the system established under paragraph (1) shall disseminate data—

subparagraph.content: on a real-time basis; and
through an application programming interface that is publicly accessible.

paragraph.heading: Complementary efforts.—
paragraph.content: The system established under paragraph (1) shall complement any existing data dissemination efforts of the Administrator that make use of electricity generation data, such as electricity demand by subregion and electricity interchange with directly interconnected balancing authorities.

subsection.heading: Observed Characteristics of Bulk Power System Resource Integration.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall establish a system to provide to the public timely data on the integration of energy resources into the bulk power system and the electric distribution grids in the United States, and the observed effects of that integration.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out paragraph (1), the Administrator shall seek to improve the temporal and spatial resolution of data relating to how grid operations are changing, such as through—

subparagraph.content: thermal generator cycling to accommodate intermittent generation;
generation unit self-scheduling practices;
renewable source curtailment;
utility-scale storage;
load response;
aggregations of distributed energy resources at the distribution system level;
power interchange between directly connected balancing authorities;
expanding Regional Transmission Organization balancing authorities;

subparagraph.chapeau: improvements in real-time—

clause.content: accuracy of locational marginal prices; and
signals to flexible demand; and135 STAT. 1041

subparagraph.content: disruptions to grid operations, including disruptions caused by cyber sources, physical sources, extreme weather events, or other sources.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall establish a system to provide to the public timely data on the operations of load-serving entities in the electricity grids of the United States.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In carrying out paragraph (1), the Administrator shall—

clause.chapeau: not less frequently than annually, provide data on—

subclause.content: the delivered generation resource mix for each load-serving entity; and
the distributed energy resources operating within each service area of a load-serving entity;

clause.content: harmonize the data on delivered generation resource mix described in clause (i)(I) with measurements of greenhouse gas emissions collected by the Environmental Protection Agency;
to the maximum extent practicable, disseminate the data described in clause (i)(I) and the harmonized data described in clause (ii) on a real-time basis; and
provide historical data, beginning with the earliest calendar year practicable, but not later than calendar year 2020, on the delivered generation resource mix described in clause (i)(I).

subparagraph.heading: Data on the delivered generation resource mix.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In collecting the data described in subparagraph (A)(i)(I), the Administrator shall—

clause.content: use existing voluntary industry methodologies, including reporting protocols, databases, and emissions and energy use tracking software that provide consistent, timely, and accessible carbon emissions intensity rates for delivered electricity;
consider that generation and transmission entities may provide data on behalf of load-serving entities;

to the extent that the Administrator determines necessary, and in a manner designed to protect confidential information, require each load-serving entity to submit additional information as needed to determine the delivered generation resource mix of the load-serving entity, including financial or contractual agreements for power and generation resource type attributes with respect to power owned by or retired by the load-serving entity; and

for any portion of the generation resource mix of a load-serving entity that is otherwise unaccounted for, develop a methodology to assign to the load-serving entity a share of the otherwise unaccounted for resource mix of the relevant balancing authority.135 STAT. 1042

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall implement measures to expand the Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey, the Commercial Building Energy Consumption Survey, and the Residential Energy Consumption Survey to include data on energy end use in order to facilitate the identification of—

paragraph.content: opportunities to improve energy efficiency and energy productivity;
changing patterns of energy use; and
opportunities to better understand and manage miscellaneous electric loads.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out subsection (a), the Administrator shall—

subparagraph.content: increase the scope and frequency of data collection on energy end uses and services;

subparagraph.chapeau: use new data collection methods and tools in order to obtain more comprehensive data and reduce the burden on survey respondents, including by—

clause.content: accessing other existing data sources; and
if feasible, developing online and real-time reporting systems;

subparagraph.chapeau: identify and report community-level economic and environmental impacts, including with respect to—

clause.content: the reliability and security of the energy supply; and
local areas with households with a high energy burden; and

subparagraph.chapeau: improve the presentation of data, including by—

clause.content: enabling the presentation of data in an interactive cartographic format on a national, regional, State, and local level with the functionality of viewing various economic, energy, and demographic measures on an individual basis or in combination; and
incorporating the results of the data collection, methods, and tools described in subparagraphs (A) and (B) into existing and new digital distribution methods.

paragraph.heading: Manufacturing energy consumption survey.—
paragraph.chapeau: With respect to the Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey, the Administrator shall—

subparagraph.content: implement measures to provide more detailed representations of data by region;

for large manufacturing facilities, break out process heat use by required process temperatures in order to facilitate the identification of opportunities for cost reductions and energy efficiency or energy productivity improvements;

subparagraph.chapeau: collect information on—

clause.content: energy source-switching capabilities, especially with respect to thermal processes and the efficiency of thermal processes;
the use of electricity, biofuels, hydrogen, or other alternative fuels to produce process heat; and
the use of demand response; and

subparagraph.chapeau: identify current and potential future industrial clusters in which multiple firms and facilities in a defined 135 STAT. 1043 geographic area share the costs and benefits of infrastructure for clean manufacturing, such as—

clause.content: hydrogen generation, production, transport, use, and storage infrastructure; and
carbon dioxide capture, transport, use, and storage infrastructure.

paragraph.heading: Residential energy consumption survey.—
paragraph.chapeau: With respect to the Residential Energy Consumption Survey, the Administrator shall—

subparagraph.chapeau: implement measures to provide more detailed representations of data by—

clause.content: geographic area, including by State (for each State);
building type, including multi-family buildings;
household income;
location in a rural area; and
other demographic characteristics, as determined by the Administrator; and

subparagraph.chapeau: report measures of—

clause.content: household electrical service capacity;
access to utility demand-side management programs and bill credits;
characteristics of the energy mix used to generate electricity in different regions; and

clause.chapeau: the household energy burden for households—

subclause.content: in different geographic areas;
by electricity, heating, and other end-uses; and

subclause.chapeau: with different demographic characteristics that correlate with increased household energy burden, including—

item.content: having a low household income;
being a minority household;
residing in manufactured or multifamily housing;
being in a fixed or retirement income household;
residing in rental housing; and
other factors, as determined by the Administrator.

section.heading: DATA COLLECTION ON ELECTRIC VEHICLE INTEGRATION WITH THE ELECTRICITY GRIDS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall develop and implement measures to expand data collection with respect to electric vehicle integration with the electricity grids.

subsection.heading: Sources of Data.—
subsection.chapeau: The sources of the data collected pursuant to subsection (a) may include—

paragraph.content: host-owned or charging-network-owned electric vehicle charging stations;
aggregators of charging-network electricity demand;
electric utilities offering managed-charging programs;
individual, corporate, or public owners of electric vehicles; and

paragraph.chapeau: balancing authority analyses of—

subparagraph.content: transformer loading congestion; and135 STAT. 1044
distribution-system congestion.

subsection.heading: Consultation and Coordination.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out subsection (a), the Administrator may consult and enter into agreements with other institutions having relevant data and data collection capabilities, such as—

paragraph.content: the Secretary of Transportation;
the Secretary;
the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency;
States or State agencies; and
private entities.

section.heading: PLAN FOR THE MODELING AND FORECASTING OF DEMAND FOR MINERALS USED IN THE ENERGY SECTOR.

paragraph.heading:
Deadline.
Coordination.In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator, in coordination with the Director of the United States Geological Survey, shall develop a plan for the modeling and forecasting of demand for energy technologies, including for energy production, transmission, or storage purposes, that use minerals that are or could be designated as critical minerals.

paragraph.heading: Inclusions.—
paragraph.chapeau: The plan developed under paragraph (1) shall identify—

subparagraph.content: the type and quantity of minerals consumed, delineated by energy technology;
existing markets for manufactured energy-producing, energy-transmission, and energy-storing equipment; and
emerging or potential markets for new energy-producing, energy-transmission, and energy-storing technologies entering commercialization.

subsection.heading: Metrics.—
subsection.chapeau: The plan developed under subsection (a)(1) shall produce forecasts of energy technology demand—

paragraph.content: over the 1-year, 5-year, and 10-year periods beginning on the date on which development of the plan is completed;
by economic sector; and

according to any other parameters that the Administrator, in collaboration with the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the United States Geological Survey, determines are needed for the Annual Critical Minerals Outlook.

subsection.heading: Collaboration.—
subsection.chapeau: The Administrator shall develop the plan under subsection (a)(1) in consultation with—

paragraph.content: the Secretary with respect to the possible trajectories of emerging energy-producing and energy-storing technologies; and

paragraph.chapeau: the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the United States Geological Survey—

subparagraph.content: to ensure coordination;
to avoid duplicative effort; and

to align the analysis of demand with data and analysis of where the minerals are produced, refined, and subsequently processed into materials and parts that are used to build energy technologies.135 STAT. 1045

subsection.heading: Deadline.In General.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall implement measures to expand and improve the international energy data resources of the Energy Information Administration in order to understand—

paragraph.content: the production and use of energy in various countries;
changing patterns of energy use internationally;
the relative costs and environmental impacts of energy production and use internationally; and
plans for or construction of major energy facilities or infrastructure.

subsection.heading: Requirements.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out subsection (a), the Administrator shall—

paragraph.content: work with, and leverage the data resources of, the International Energy Agency;
include detail on energy consumption by fuel, economic sector, and end use within countries for which data are available;

paragraph.chapeau: collect relevant measures of energy use, including—

subparagraph.content: cost; and
emissions intensity; and

paragraph.content: provide tools that allow for straightforward country-to-country comparisons of energy production and consumption across economic sectors and end uses.

section.heading: PLAN FOR THE NATIONAL ENERGY MODELING SYSTEM.
section.chapeau: Deadline.Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall develop a plan to identify any need or opportunity to update or further the capabilities of the National Energy Modeling System, including with respect to—

paragraph.content: treating energy demand endogenously;
increased natural gas usage and increased market penetration of renewable energy;
flexible operating modes of nuclear power plants, such as load following and frequency control;

tools to model multiple-output energy systems that provide hydrogen, high-value heat, electricity, and chemical synthesis services, including interactions of those energy systems with the electricity grids, pipeline networks, and the broader economy;
demand response and improved representation of energy storage, including long-duration storage, in capacity expansion models;
electrification, particularly with respect to the transportation, industrial, and buildings sectors;
increasing model resolution to represent all hours of the year and all electricity generators;

paragraph.chapeau: wholesale electricity market design and the appropriate valuation of all services that support the reliability of electricity grids, such as—

subparagraph.content: battery storage; and
synthetic inertia from grid-tied inverters;

paragraph.content: economic modeling of the role of energy efficiency, demand response, electricity storage, and a variety of distributed generation technologies;
the production, transport, use, and storage of carbon dioxide, hydrogen, and hydrogen carriers;135 STAT. 1046

paragraph.chapeau: greater flexibility in—

subparagraph.chapeau: the modeling of the environmental impacts of electricity systems, such as—

clause.content: emissions of greenhouse gases and other pollutants; and
the use of land and water resources; and

subparagraph.content: the ability to support climate modeling, such as the climate modeling performed by the Office of Biological and Environmental Research in the Office of Science of the Department;

paragraph.chapeau: technologies that are in an early stage of commercial deployment and have been identified by the Secretary as candidates for large-scale demonstration projects, such as—

subparagraph.content: carbon capture, transport, use, and storage from any source or economic sector;
direct air capture;
hydrogen production, including via electrolysis;
synthetic and biogenic hydrocarbon liquid and gaseous fuels;
supercritical carbon dioxide combustion turbines;
industrial fuel cell and hydrogen combustion equipment; and
industrial electric boilers;

paragraph.chapeau: increased and improved data sources and tools, including—

subparagraph.content: the establishment of technology and cost baselines, including technology learning rates;
economic and employment impacts of energy system policies and energy prices on households, as a function of household income and region; and
the use of behavioral economics to inform demand modeling in all sectors; and

paragraph.chapeau: striving to migrate toward a single, consistent, and open-source modeling platform, and increasing open access to model systems, data, and outcomes, for—

subparagraph.content: disseminating reference scenarios that can be transparently and broadly replicated; and
promoting the development of the researcher and analyst workforce needed to continue the development and validation of improved energy system models in the future.

section.heading: REPORT ON COSTS OF CARBON ABATEMENT IN THE ELECTRICITY SECTOR.
section.chapeau: Not later than 270 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall submit to Congress a report on—

paragraph.content: the potential use of levelized cost of carbon abatement or a similar metric in analyzing generators of electricity, including an identification of limitations and appropriate uses of the metric;

paragraph.chapeau: the feasibility and impact of incorporating levelized cost of carbon abatement in long-term forecasts—

subparagraph.content: to compare technical approaches and understand real-time changes in fossil-fuel and nuclear dispatch;
to compare the system-level costs of technology options to reduce emissions; and135 STAT. 1047
to compare the costs of policy options, including current policies, regarding valid and verifiable reductions and removals of carbon; and

subparagraph.chapeau: a potential process to measure carbon dioxide emissions intensity per unit of output production for a range of—

clause.content: energy sources;
sectors; and
geographic regions; and

subparagraph.content: a corresponding process to provide an empirical framework for reporting the status and costs of carbon dioxide reduction relative to specified goals.

section.heading: HARMONIZATION OF EFFORTS AND DATA.
section.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall establish a system to harmonize, to the maximum extent practicable and consistent with data integrity—

paragraph.chapeau: the data collection efforts of the Administrator, including any data collection required under this subtitle, with the data collection efforts of—

subparagraph.content: the Environmental Protection Agency, as the Administrator determines to be appropriate;
other relevant Federal agencies, as the Administrator determines to be appropriate; and
State or regional energy credit registries, as the Administrator determines to be appropriate;

paragraph.content: the data collected under this subtitle, including the operating data on electricity generation collected under section 40412(a), with data collected by the entities described in subparagraphs (A) through (C) of paragraph (1), including any measurements of greenhouse gas and other pollutant emissions collected by the Environmental Protection Agency, as the Administrator determines to be appropriate; and

the efforts of the Administrator to identify and report relevant impacts, opportunities, and patterns with respect to energy use, including the identification of community-level economic and environmental impacts required under section 40413(b)(1)(C), with the efforts of the Environmental Protection Agency and other relevant Federal agencies, as determined by the Administrator, to identify similar impacts, opportunities, and patterns.

section.heading: CONSIDERATION OF MEASURES TO PROMOTE GREATER ELECTRIFICATION OF THE TRANSPORTATION SECTOR.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content:
Section 111(d) of the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2621(d)) (as amended by section 40104(a)(1)) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(21) Electric vehicle charging programs.—Each State shall consider measures to promote greater electrification of the transportation sector, including the establishment of rates that—“(A) promote affordable and equitable electric vehicle charging options for residential, commercial, and public electric vehicle charging infrastructure;135 STAT. 1048 “(B) improve the customer experience associated with electric vehicle charging, including by reducing charging times for light-, medium-, and heavy-duty vehicles; “(C) accelerate third-party investment in electric vehicle charging for light-, medium-, and heavy-duty vehicles; and “(D) appropriately recover the marginal costs of delivering electricity to electric vehicles and electric vehicle charging infrastructure.”
.

paragraph.heading: Time limitation.—
paragraph.content:
Section 112(b) of the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2622(b)) (as amended by section 40104(a)(2)(A)) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(8)(A)
Deadlines.Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this paragraph, each State regulatory authority (with respect to each electric utility for which the State has ratemaking authority) and each nonregulated utility shall commence consideration under section 111, or set a hearing date for consideration, with respect to the standard established by paragraph (21) of section 111(d). “(B) Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this paragraph, each State regulatory authority (with respect to each electric utility for which the State has ratemaking authority), and each nonregulated electric utility shall complete the consideration and make the determination under section 111 with respect to the standard established by paragraph (21) of section 111(d).”
.

paragraph.heading: Failure to comply.—
paragraph.content: Section 112(c) of the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2622(c)) (as amended by section 40104(a)(2)(B)(i)) is amended by adding at the end the following: “In the case of the standard established by paragraph (21) of section 111(d), the reference contained in this subsection to the date of enactment of this Act shall be deemed to be a reference to the date of enactment of that paragraph (21).”.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content:
Section 112 of the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2622) (as amended by section 40104(a)(2)(C)(i)) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(h) Other Prior State Actions.—Subsections (b) and (c) shall not apply to the standard established by paragraph (21) of section 111(d) in the case of any electric utility in a State if, before the date of enactment of this subsection—“(1) the State has implemented for the electric utility the standard (or a comparable standard); “(2) the State regulatory authority for the State or the relevant nonregulated electric utility has conducted a proceeding to consider implementation of the standard (or a comparable standard) for the electric utility; or “(3)
Time period.the State legislature has voted on the implementation of the standard (or a comparable standard) for the electric utility during the 3-year period ending on that date of enactment.”
.

subparagraph.heading: Cross-reference.—
subparagraph.content: Section 124 of the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2634) 135 STAT. 1049 (as amended by section 40104(a)(2)(C)(ii)(II)) is amended by adding at the end the following: “In the case of the standard established by paragraph (21) of section 111(d), the reference contained in this section to the date of enactment of this Act shall be deemed to be a reference to the date of enactment of that paragraph (21).”.

section.heading: OFFICE OF PUBLIC PARTICIPATION.
section.chapeau: Section 319 of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 825q–1) is amended—

paragraph.chapeau: in subsection (a)(2)—

subparagraph.content: in subparagraph (A), by striking the third sentence; and

subparagraph.chapeau: in subparagraph (B)—

clause.content: by striking the third sentence and inserting the following: “The Director shall be compensated at a rate of pay not greater than the maximum rate of pay prescribed for a senior executive in the Senior Executive Service under section 5382 of title 5, United States Code.”; and
by striking the first sentence; and

paragraph.content: in subsection (b), by striking paragraph (4).

subsection.heading:
Consultation.
Assessments.In General.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, in consultation with appropriate Federal agencies and relevant stakeholders, shall submit to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives a report that assesses using digital tools and platforms as climate solutions, including—

paragraph.content: artificial intelligence and machine learning;
blockchain technologies and distributed ledgers;
crowdsourcing platforms;
the Internet of Things;
distributed computing for the grid; and
software and systems.

subsection.heading: Contents.—
subsection.chapeau: The report required under subsection (a) shall include—

paragraph.content: as practicable, a full inventory and assessment of digital climate solutions;
an analysis of how the private sector can utilize the digital tools and platforms included in the inventory under paragraph (1) to accelerate digital climate solutions; and

a summary of opportunities to enhance the standardization of voluntary and regulatory climate disclosure protocols, including enabling the data to be disseminated through an application programming interface that is accessible to the public.

section.heading: STUDY AND REPORT BY THE SECRETARY OF ENERGY ON JOB LOSS AND IMPACTS ON CONSUMER ENERGY COSTS DUE TO THE REVOCATION OF THE PERMIT FOR THE KEYSTONE XL PIPELINE.

subsection.heading: Definition of Executive Order.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “Executive Order” means Executive Order 13990 (86 Fed. Reg. 7037; relating to protecting public health and the environment and restoring science to tackle the climate crisis).135 STAT. 1050

subsection.heading: Study and Report.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

paragraph.chapeau:
Estimates.
Time period.conduct a study to estimate—

subparagraph.content: the total number of jobs that were lost as a direct or indirect result of section 6 of the Executive Order over the 10-year period beginning on the date on which the Executive Order was issued; and

the impact on consumer energy costs that are projected to result as a direct or indirect result of section 6 of the Executive Order over the 10-year period beginning on the date on which the Executive Order was issued; and

paragraph.content: not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, submit to Congress a report describing the findings of the study conducted under paragraph (1).

section.heading: STUDY ON IMPACT OF ELECTRIC VEHICLES.
section.content: Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall conduct, and submit to Congress a report describing the results of, a study on the cradle to grave environmental impact of electric vehicles.

section.heading: STUDY ON IMPACT OF FORCED LABOR IN CHINA ON THE ELECTRIC VEHICLE SUPPLY CHAIN.
section.content: Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, in coordination with the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Commerce, shall study the impact of forced labor in China on the electric vehicle supply chain.

section.heading: DEFINITIONS.
section.chapeau: In this subtitle:

paragraph.heading: Priority state.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “priority State” means a State that—

subparagraph.content: is eligible for funding under the State Energy Program; and

clause.content: is among the 15 States with the highest annual per-capita combined residential and commercial sector energy consumption, as most recently reported by the Energy Information Administration; or
is among the 15 States with the highest annual per-capita energy-related carbon dioxide emissions by State, as most recently reported by the Energy Information Administration.

paragraph.heading: Program.—
paragraph.content: The term “program” means the program established under section 40502(a).

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means a State (as defined in section 3 of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (42 U.S.C. 6202)), acting through a State energy office.

paragraph.heading: State energy program.—
paragraph.content: The term “State Energy Program” means the State Energy Program established under 135 STAT. 1051 part D of title III of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (42 U.S.C. 6321 et seq.).

section.heading: ENERGY EFFICIENCY REVOLVING LOAN FUND CAPITALIZATION GRANT PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, under the State Energy Program, the Secretary shall establish a program under which the Secretary shall provide capitalization grants to States to establish a revolving loan fund under which the State shall provide loans and grants, as applicable, in accordance with this section.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Of the amounts made available under subsection (j), the Secretary shall use 40 percent to provide capitalization grants to States that are eligible for funding under the State Energy Program, in accordance with the allocation formula established under section 420.11 of title 10, Code of Federal Regulations (or successor regulations).

subparagraph.heading: Remaining funding.—
subparagraph.content: After applying the allocation formula described in subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall redistribute any unclaimed funds to the remaining States seeking capitalization grants under that subparagraph.

subparagraph.heading: Determination.In general.—
subparagraph.content: Of the amounts made available under subsection (j), the Secretary shall use 60 percent to provide supplemental capitalization grants to priority States in accordance with an allocation formula determined by the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Remaining funding.—
subparagraph.content: After applying the allocation formula described in subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall redistribute any unclaimed funds to the remaining priority States seeking supplemental capitalization grants under that subparagraph.

clause.heading: Maximum amount.—
clause.content: The amount of a supplemental capitalization grant provided to a State under this paragraph shall not exceed $15,000,000.

clause.heading: Supplement not supplant.—
clause.content: A supplemental capitalization grant received by a State under this paragraph shall supplement, not supplant, a capitalization grant received by that State under paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Applications for Capitalization Grants.—
subsection.chapeau: A State seeking a capitalization grant under the program shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require, including—

paragraph.content: a detailed explanation of how the grant will be used, including a plan to establish a new revolving loan fund or use an existing revolving loan fund;
the need of eligible recipients for loans and grants in the State for assistance with conducting energy audits;
a description of the expected benefits that building infrastructure and energy system upgrades and retrofits will have on communities in the State; and135 STAT. 1052
in the case of a priority State seeking a supplemental capitalization grant under subsection (b)(2), a justification for needing the supplemental funding.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish a timeline with dates by, or periods by the end of, which a State shall—

subparagraph.content: on receipt of a capitalization grant under the program, deposit the grant funds into a revolving loan fund; and
begin using the capitalization grant as described in subsection (e)(1).

paragraph.heading:
Use
Requirement.
Deadline. of grant.—
paragraph.content: Under the timeline established under paragraph (1), a State shall be required to begin using a capitalization grant not more than 180 days after the date on which the grant is received.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: A State that receives a capitalization grant under the program—

subparagraph.content: Loans.shall provide loans in accordance with paragraph (2); and
may provide grants in accordance with paragraph (3).

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: A State that receives a capitalization grant under the program may provide a loan to an eligible recipient described in clause (iv) to conduct a commercial energy audit.

clause.heading: Audit requirements.—
clause.chapeau: A commercial energy audit conducted using a loan provided under clause (i) shall—

subclause.content: Determination.determine the overall consumption of energy of the facility of the eligible recipient;

subclause.chapeau:
Recommenda-
tions.identify and recommend lifecycle cost-effective opportunities to reduce the energy consumption of the facility of the eligible recipient, including through energy efficient—

item.content: lighting;
heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems;
windows;
appliances; and
insulation and building envelopes;

subclause.content: estimate the energy and cost savings potential of the opportunities identified in subclause (II) using software approved by the Secretary;

subclause.chapeau: identify—

item.content: the period and level of peak energy demand for each building within the facility of the eligible recipient; and
the sources of energy consumption that are contributing the most to that period of peak energy demand;

subclause.content:
Recommenda-
tion.recommend controls and management systems to reduce or redistribute peak energy consumption; and135 STAT. 1053

Cost estimate.estimate the total energy and cost savings potential for the facility of the eligible recipient if all recommended upgrades and retrofits are implemented, using software approved by the Secretary.

clause.heading: Additional audit inclusions.—
clause.content: A commercial energy audit conducted using a loan provided under clause (i) may recommend strategies to increase energy efficiency of the facility of the eligible recipient through use of electric systems or other high-efficiency systems utilizing fuels, including natural gas and hydrogen.

clause.heading: Eligible recipients.—
clause.chapeau: An eligible recipient under clause (i) is a business that—

subclause.content: conducts the majority of its business in the State that provides the loan under that clause; and

subclause.chapeau: owns or operates—

item.content: 1 or more commercial buildings; or
commercial space within a building that serves multiple functions, such as a building for commercial and residential operations.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: A State that receives a capitalization grant under the program may provide a loan to an eligible recipient described in clause (iv) to conduct a residential energy audit.

clause.heading: Residential energy audit requirements.—
clause.chapeau: A residential energy audit conducted using a loan under clause (i) shall—

subclause.content: utilize the same evaluation criteria as the Home Performance Assessment used in the Energy Star program established under section 324A of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (42 U.S.C. 6294a);

subclause.chapeau: recommend lifecycle cost-effective opportunities to reduce energy consumption within the residential building of the eligible recipient, including through energy efficient—

item.content: lighting;
heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems;
windows;
appliances; and
insulation and building envelopes;

subclause.content:
Recommenda-
tion.recommend controls and management systems to reduce or redistribute peak energy consumption;
compare the energy consumption of the residential building of the eligible recipient to comparable residential buildings in the same geographic area; and

Determination.provide a Home Energy Score, or equivalent score (as determined by the Secretary), for the residential building of the eligible recipient by using the Home Energy Score Tool of the Department or an equivalent scoring tool.135 STAT. 1054

clause.heading: Additional audit inclusions.—
clause.content: A residential energy audit conducted using a loan provided under clause (i) may recommend strategies to increase energy efficiency of the facility of the eligible recipient through use of electric systems or other high-efficiency systems utilizing fuels, including natural gas and hydrogen.

clause.heading: Eligible recipients.—
clause.chapeau: An eligible recipient under clause (i) is—

subclause.chapeau: an individual who owns—

item.content: a single family home;
a condominium or duplex; or
a manufactured housing unit; or

subclause.content: a business that owns or operates a multifamily housing facility.

subparagraph.heading: Commercial and residential energy upgrades and retrofits.—

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: A State that receives a capitalization grant under the program may provide a loan to an eligible recipient described in clause (ii) to carry out upgrades or retrofits of building infrastructure and systems that—

subclause.content: are recommended in the commercial energy audit or residential energy audit, as applicable, completed for the building or facility of the eligible recipient;
satisfy at least 1 of the criteria in the Home Performance Assessment used in the Energy Star program established under section 324A of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (42 U.S.C. 6294a);

subclause.chapeau: improve, with respect to the building or facility of the eligible recipient—

item.content: the physical comfort of the building or facility occupants;
the energy efficiency of the building or facility; or
the quality of the air in the building or facility; and
are lifecycle cost-effective; and

subitem.content: reduce the energy intensity of the building or facility of the eligible recipient; or
improve the control and management of energy usage of the building or facility to reduce demand during peak times.

clause.heading: Eligible recipients.—
clause.chapeau: An eligible recipient under clause (i) is an eligible recipient described in subparagraph (A)(iv) or (B)(iv) that—

subclause.content: has completed a commercial energy audit described in subparagraph (A) or a residential energy audit described in subparagraph (B) using a loan provided under the applicable subparagraph; or

subclause.chapeau: has completed a commercial energy audit or residential energy audit that—

item.content: was not funded by a loan under this paragraph; and135 STAT. 1055

subitem.content: meets the requirements for the applicable audit under subparagraph (A) or (B), as applicable; or
the Secretary determines is otherwise satisfactory.

subclause.heading: In general.—
subclause.chapeau: A loan provided under this subparagraph shall be required to be fully amortized by the earlier of—

item.content: subject to subclause (II), the year in which the upgrades or retrofits carried out using the loan exceed their expected useful life; and
Time period.15 years after those upgrades or retrofits are installed.

subclause.heading: Calculation.—
subclause.content: For purposes of subclause (I)(aa), in the case of a loan being used to fund multiple upgrades or retrofits, the longest-lived upgrade or retrofit shall be used to calculate the year in which the upgrades or retrofits carried out using the loan exceed their expected useful life.

subparagraph.heading: Referral to qualified contractors.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Following the completion of an audit under subparagraph (A) or (B) by an eligible recipient of a loan under the applicable subparagraph, the State may refer the eligible recipient to a qualified contractor, as determined by the State, to estimate—

clause.content: the upfront capital cost of each recommended upgrade; and
the total upfront capital cost of implementing all recommended upgrades.

subparagraph.heading: Loan recipients.—
subparagraph.content: Each State providing loans under this paragraph shall, to the maximum extent practicable, provide loans to eligible recipients that do not have access to private capital.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: A State that receives a capitalization grant under the program may use not more than 25 percent of the grant funds to provide grants or technical assistance to eligible entities described in subparagraph (B) to carry out the activities described in subparagraphs (A), (B), and (C) of paragraph (2).

subparagraph.heading: Eligible entity.—
subparagraph.chapeau: An entity eligible for a grant or technical assistance under subparagraph (A) is—

clause.chapeau: a business that—

subclause.content: is an eligible recipient described in paragraph (2)(A)(iv); and
has fewer than 500 employees; or

clause.content: a low-income individual (as defined in section 3 of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (29 U.S.C. 3102)) that owns a residential building.

paragraph.heading: Deadline.Final assessment.—
paragraph.content: A State that provides a capitalization grant under paragraph (2)(C) to an eligible recipient described in clause (ii) of that paragraph may, not later than 1 year after the date on which the upgrades or retrofits funded by the grant under that paragraph are completed, provide 135 STAT. 1056 to the eligible recipient a loan or, in accordance with paragraph (3), a grant to conduct a final energy audit that assesses the total energy savings from the upgrades or retrofits.

paragraph.heading: Administrative expenses.—
paragraph.content: A State that receives a capitalization grant under the program may use not more than 10 percent of the grant funds for administrative expenses.

subsection.heading: Coordination With Existing Programs.—
subsection.content: A State receiving a capitalization grant under the program is encouraged to utilize and build on existing programs and infrastructure within the State that may aid the State in carrying out a revolving loan fund program.

subsection.heading: Leveraging Private Capital.—
subsection.content: A State receiving a capitalization grant under the program shall, to the maximum extent practicable, use the grant to leverage private capital.

subsection.heading: Outreach.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall engage in outreach to inform States of the availability of capitalization grants under the program.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Each State that receives a capitalization grant under the program shall, not later than 2 years after a grant is received, submit to the Secretary a report that describes—

paragraph.chapeau: the number of recipients to which the State has distributed—

subparagraph.chapeau: loans for—

clause.content: commercial energy audits under subsection (e)(2)(A);
residential energy audits under subsection (e)(2)(B);
energy upgrades and retrofits under subsection (e)(2)(C); and

subparagraph.content: grants under subsection (e)(3); and

paragraph.content: the average capital cost of upgrades and retrofits across all commercial energy audits and residential energy audits that were conducted in the State using loans provided by the State under subsection (e).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $250,000,000 for fiscal year 2022, to remain available until expended.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Covered certification.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “covered certification” means any of the following certifications:

subparagraph.content: The American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers Building Energy Assessment Professional certification.
The Association of Energy Engineers Certified Energy Auditor certification.
The Building Performance Institute Home Energy Professional Energy Auditor certification.
The Residential Energy Services Network Home Energy Rater certification.
Any other third-party certification recognized by the Department.
Any third-party certification that the Secretary determines is equivalent to the certifications described in subparagraphs (A) through (E).135 STAT. 1057

paragraph.heading: Eligible state.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible State” means a State that—

subparagraph.content: has a demonstrated need for assistance for training energy auditors; and
meets any additional criteria determined necessary by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: Under the State Energy Program, the Secretary shall establish a competitive grant program under which the Secretary shall award grants to eligible States to train individuals to conduct energy audits or surveys of commercial and residential buildings.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: A State seeking a grant under subsection (b) shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require, including the energy auditor training program plan described in paragraph (2).

paragraph.heading: Energy auditor training program plan.—
paragraph.chapeau: An energy auditor training program plan submitted with an application under paragraph (1) shall include—

clause.content: a proposed training curriculum for energy audit trainees; and
an identification of the covered certification that those trainees will receive on completion of that training curriculum;

subparagraph.content: the expected per-individual cost of training;
a plan for connecting trainees with employment opportunities; and
any additional information required by the Secretary.
