clause.content: shall acknowledge receipt;

clause.chapeau: if the final proposal is complete—

subclause.chapeau: Determinations.shall determine whether the use of funds proposed in the final proposal—

item.content: complies with subsection (f);
is in the public interest; and
effectuates the purposes of this Act;

subclause.content: shall approve or disapprove the final proposal based on the determinations under subclause (I); and

if the Assistant Secretary approves the final proposal under clause (ii)(II), shall make available to the eligible entity the remainder of the grant funds allocated to the eligible entity under subsection (c); and

clause.content: Notification.if the final proposal is incomplete, or is disapproved under clause (ii)(II), shall notify the eligible entity and provide the eligible entity with an opportunity to resubmit the final proposal.

subparagraph.heading: Consideration of resubmitted final proposal.—
subparagraph.chapeau: After receipt of a resubmitted final proposal for a grant under this paragraph, the Assistant Secretary—

clause.content: shall acknowledge receipt;

clause.chapeau: if the final proposal is complete—

subclause.chapeau: Determinations.shall determine whether the use of funds proposed in the final proposal—

item.content: complies with subsection (f);
is in the public interest; and
effectuates the purposes of this Act;

subclause.content: shall approve or disapprove the final proposal based on the determinations under subclause (I); and

if the Assistant Secretary approves the final proposal under clause (ii)(II), shall make available to the eligible entity the remainder of the grant funds allocated to the eligible entity under subsection (c); and

clause.content: Notification.if the final proposal is incomplete, or is disapproved under clause (ii)(II), shall notify the eligible entity and provide the eligible entity with an opportunity to resubmit the final proposal.135 STAT. 1195

subsection.heading: Use of Funds.—
subsection.chapeau: An eligible entity may use grant funds received under this section to competitively award subgrants for—

paragraph.content: unserved service projects and underserved service projects;
connecting eligible community anchor institutions;
data collection, broadband mapping, and planning;

paragraph.chapeau: installing internet and Wi-Fi infrastructure or providing reduced-cost broadband within a multi-family residential building, with priority given to a residential building that—

subparagraph.content: has a substantial share of unserved households; or

is in a location in which the percentage of individuals with a household income that is at or below 150 percent of the poverty line applicable to a family of the size involved (as determined under section 673(2) of the Community Services Block Grant Act (42 U.S.C. 9902(2)) is higher than the national percentage of such individuals;

paragraph.content: broadband adoption, including programs to provide affordable internet-capable devices; and
Determination.any use determined necessary by the Assistant Secretary to facilitate the goals of the Program.

paragraph.heading: Subgrantee obligations.—
paragraph.chapeau: A subgrantee, in carrying out activities using amounts received from an eligible entity under this section—

subparagraph.content: shall adhere to quality-of-service standards, as established by the Assistant Secretary;

Compliance.
Consultation.shall comply with prudent cybersecurity and supply chain risk management practices, as specified by the Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Commission;
shall incorporate best practices, as defined by the Assistant Secretary, for ensuring reliability and resilience of broadband infrastructure; and

subparagraph.chapeau: may not use the amounts to purchase or support—

clause.content: any covered communications equipment or service, as defined in section 9 of the Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2019 (47 U.S.C. 1608); or

fiber optic cable and optical transmission equipment manufactured in the People’s Republic of China, except that the Assistant Secretary may waive the application of this clause with respect to a project if the eligible entity that awards a subgrant for the project shows that such application would unreasonably increase the cost of the project.

paragraph.heading: Eligible entity obligations.—
paragraph.chapeau: In distributing funds to subgrantees under this section, an eligible entity shall—

subparagraph.chapeau: ensure that any prospective subgrantee—

clause.content: is capable of carrying out activities funded by the subgrant in a competent manner in compliance with all applicable Federal, State, and local laws;

clause.chapeau: has the financial and managerial capacity to meet—

subclause.content: the commitments of the subgrantee under the subgrant;135 STAT. 1196
the requirements of the Program; and
such requirements as may be further prescribed by the Assistant Secretary; and

clause.content: has the technical and operational capability to provide the services promised in the subgrant in the manner contemplated by the subgrant award;

subparagraph.content: Contracts.stipulate, in any contract with a subgrantee for the use of such funds, reasonable provisions for recovery of funds for nonperformance; and

clause.content: distribute the funds in an equitable and non-discriminatory manner; and
ensure, through a stipulation in any contract with a subgrantee for the use of such funds, that each subgrantee uses the funds in an equitable and nondiscriminatory manner.

paragraph.heading: Deobligation of awards; internet disclosure.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Assistant Secretary—

subparagraph.content: shall establish, in coordination with relevant Federal and State partners, appropriate mechanisms to ensure appropriate use of funds made available under this section;

subparagraph.chapeau: may, in addition to other authority under applicable law—

clause.chapeau: deobligate grant funds awarded to an eligible entity that—

subclause.content: violates paragraph (2); or
demonstrates an insufficient level of performance, or wasteful or fraudulent spending, as defined in advance by the Assistant Secretary; and

clause.content: award grant funds that are deobligated under clause (i) to new or existing applicants consistent with this section; and

subparagraph.content: shall create and maintain a fully searchable database, accessible on the internet at no cost to the public, that contains information sufficient to allow the public to understand and monitor grants and subgrants awarded under the Program.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: An eligible entity, in awarding subgrants for the deployment of a broadband network using grant funds received under this section, as authorized under subsection (f)(1)—

clause.chapeau: shall award funding in a manner that—

subclause.content: prioritizes unserved service projects;

after certifying to the Assistant Secretary that the eligible entity will ensure coverage of broadband service to all unserved locations within the eligible entity, prioritizes underserved service projects; and
after prioritizing underserved service projects, provides funding to connect eligible community anchor institutions;

clause.content: in providing funding under subclauses (I), (II), and (III) of clause (i), shall prioritize funding for deployment of broadband infrastructure for priority broadband projects;135 STAT. 1197

may not exclude cooperatives, nonprofit organizations, public-private partnerships, private companies, public or private utilities, public utility districts, or local governments from eligibility for such grant funds; and

clause.chapeau: shall give priority to projects based on—

subclause.content: deployment of a broadband network to persistent poverty counties or high-poverty areas;
the speeds of the proposed broadband service;
the expediency with which a project can be completed; and
a demonstrated record of and plans to be in compliance with Federal labor and employment laws.

subparagraph.heading: Authority of assistant secretary.—
subparagraph.content: The Assistant Secretary may provide additional guidance on the prioritization of subgrants awarded for the deployment of a broadband network using grant funds received under this section.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: After submitting an initial proposal under subsection (e)(3) and before allocating grant funds received under this section for the deployment of broadband networks, an eligible entity shall ensure a transparent, evidence-based, and expeditious challenge process under which a unit of local government, nonprofit organization, or other broadband service provider can challenge a determination made by the eligible entity in the initial proposal as to whether a particular location or community anchor institution within the jurisdiction of the eligible entity is eligible for the grant funds, including whether a particular location is unserved or underserved.

subparagraph.heading: Final identification; notification of funding eligibility.—
subparagraph.content:
After
Deadline.resolving each challenge under subparagraph (A), and not later than 60 days before allocating grant funds received under this section for the deployment of broadband networks, an eligible entity shall provide public notice of the final classification of each unserved location, underserved location, or eligible community anchor institution within the jurisdiction of the eligible entity.

subparagraph.heading: Notification.Consultation with ntia.—
subparagraph.content: An eligible entity shall notify the Assistant Secretary of any modification to the initial proposal of the eligible entity submitted under subsection (e)(3) that is necessitated by a successful challenge under subparagraph (A) of this paragraph.

subparagraph.heading: NTIA authority.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Assistant Secretary—

clause.content: may modify the challenge process required under subparagraph (A) as necessary; and
may reverse the determination of an eligible entity with respect to the eligibility of a particular location or community anchor institution for grant funds under this section.

clause.heading: Deadline for resolution of challenge process under broadband data act.—
clause.content: Section 802(b)(5)(C)(i) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 642(b)(5)(C)(i)) is amended by striking “challenges” and inserting the following: “challenges, which shall require that the Commission resolve a challenge not later than 90 days after the date on which a final response by a provider to a challenge to the accuracy of a map or information described in subparagraph (A) is complete”.

clause.heading: Paperwork reduction act exemption expansion.—
clause.content: Section 806(b) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 646(b)) is amended by striking “the initial rule making required under section 802(a)(1)” and inserting “any rule making or other action by the Commission required under this title”.

clause.heading: Implementation.—
clause.content: The Commission shall implement the amendments made by this subparagraph as soon as possible after the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Non-federal share of broadband infrastructure deployment costs.—

clause.heading: Matching requirement.—
clause.content: In allocating grant funds received under this section for deployment of broadband networks, an eligible entity shall provide, or require a subgrantee to provide, a contribution, derived from non-Federal funds (or funds from a Federal regional commission or authority), except in high-cost areas or as otherwise provided by this Act, of not less than 25 percent of project costs.

clause.heading: Waiver.—
clause.content: Upon request by an eligible entity or a subgrantee, the Assistant Secretary may reduce or waive the required matching contribution under clause (i).

subparagraph.heading: Source of match.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A matching contribution under subparagraph (A)—

clause.content: may be provided by an eligible entity, a unit of local government, a utility company, a cooperative, a nonprofit organization, a for-profit company, regional planning or governmental organization, a Federal regional commission or authority, or any combination thereof;
may include in-kind contributions; and

clause.chapeau: may include funds that were provided to an eligible entity or a subgrantee—

subclause.chapeau: under—

item.content: the Families First Coronavirus Response Act (Public Law 116–127; 134 Stat. 178);
the CARES Act (Public Law 116–136; 134 Stat. 281);
the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (Public Law 116–260; 134 Stat. 1182);
the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (Public Law 117–2; 135 Stat. 4); or135 STAT. 1199
any amendment made by an Act described in any of items (aa) through (dd); and

subclause.content: for the purpose of deployment of broadband service, as described in the applicable provision of law described in subclause (I).

subparagraph.heading: Definition.—
subparagraph.chapeau: For purposes of this paragraph, the term “Federal regional commission or authority” means—

clause.content: the Appalachian Regional Commission;
the Delta Regional Authority;
the Denali Commission; and
the Northern Border Regional Commission.

paragraph.heading: Deployment and provision of service requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: An entity that receives a subgrant under subsection (f)(1) for the deployment of a broadband network—

subparagraph.chapeau: in providing broadband service using the network—

clause.chapeau: shall provide broadband service—

subclause.content: at a speed of not less than 100 megabits per second for downloads and 20 megabits per second for uploads;
with a latency that is sufficiently low to allow reasonably foreseeable, real-time, interactive applications; and
Time period.with network outages that do not exceed, on average, 48 hours over any 365-day period; and

clause.content: shall provide access to broadband service to each customer served by the project that desires broadband service;

subparagraph.content: shall offer not less than 1 low-cost broadband service option for eligible subscribers, as those terms are defined in paragraph (5) of this subsection;

subparagraph.chapeau: shall deploy the broadband network and begin providing broadband service to each customer that desires broadband service not later than 4 years after the date on which the entity receives the subgrant, except that an eligible entity may extend the deadline under this subparagraph if—

clause.content: the eligible entity has a plan for use of the grant funds;
the construction project is underway; or
extenuating circumstances require an extension of time to allow the project to be completed;

subparagraph.content: for any project that involves laying fiber optic cables or conduit underground or along a roadway, shall include interspersed conduit access points at regular and short intervals;

may use the subgrant to deploy broadband infrastructure in or through any area required to reach interconnection points or otherwise to ensure the technical feasibility and financial sustainability of a project providing broadband service to an unserved location, underserved location, or eligible community anchor institution;

Public information.
Web posting.once the network has been deployed, shall provide public notice, online and through other means, of that fact to the locations and areas to which broadband service 135 STAT. 1200 has been provided and share the public notice with the eligible entity that awarded the subgrant;

shall carry out public awareness campaigns in service areas that are designed to highlight the value and benefits of broadband service in order to increase the adoption of broadband service by consumers; and

if the entity is no longer able to provide broadband service to the locations covered by the subgrant at any time, shall sell the network capacity at a reasonable, wholesale rate on a nondiscriminatory basis to other broadband service providers or public sector entities.

subparagraph.heading: Definitions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In this paragraph—

clause.content: the term “eligible subscriber” shall have the meaning given the term by the Assistant Secretary for purposes of this paragraph; and
the term “low-cost broadband service option” shall be defined by an eligible entity for subgrantees of the eligible entity in accordance with subparagraph (B).

clause.heading: Proposal.—
clause.content: An eligible entity shall submit to the Assistant Secretary for approval, in the final proposal of the eligible entity submitted under subsection (e)(4), a proposed definition of “low-cost broadband service option” that shall apply to subgrantees of the eligible entity for purposes of the requirement under paragraph (4)(B) of this subsection.

clause.heading: Consultation.—
clause.content: An eligible entity shall consult with the Assistant Secretary and prospective subgrantees regarding a proposed definition of “low-cost broadband service option” before submitting the proposed definition to the Assistant Secretary under clause (i).

subclause.heading: Effective date.In general.—
subclause.content: A proposed definition of “low-cost broadband service option” submitted by an eligible entity under clause (i) shall not take effect until the Assistant Secretary approves the final proposal of the eligible entity submitted under subsection (e)(4), including approval of the proposed definition of “low-cost broadband service option”.

subclause.heading: Resubmission.—
subclause.chapeau: If the Assistant Secretary does not approve a proposed definition of “low-cost broadband service option” submitted by an eligible entity under clause (i), the Assistant Secretary shall—

item.content: notify the eligible entity and provide the eligible entity with an opportunity to resubmit the final proposal, as provided in subsection (e)(4), with an improved definition of “low-cost broadband service option”; and
provide the eligible entity with instructions on how to cure the defects in the proposed definition.135 STAT. 1201

clause.heading: Public disclosure.—
clause.content: After the Assistant Secretary approves the final proposal of an eligible entity under subsection (e)(4), and before the Assistant Secretary disburses any funds to the eligible entity based on that approval, the Assistant Secretary shall publicly disclose the eligible entity’s definition of “low-cost broadband service option”.

subparagraph.heading: Procedures.Nonperformance.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Assistant Secretary shall develop procedures under which the Assistant Secretary or an eligible entity may—

clause.content: evaluate the compliance of a subgrantee with the requirement under paragraph (4)(B); and
take corrective action, including recoupment of funds from the subgrantee, for noncompliance with the requirement under paragraph (4)(B).

subparagraph.heading: No regulation of rates permitted.—
subparagraph.content: Nothing in this title may be construed to authorize the Assistant Secretary or the National Telecommunications and Information Administration to regulate the rates charged for broadband service.

subparagraph.heading: Guidance.—
subparagraph.content: The Assistant Secretary may issue guidance to eligible entities to carry out the purposes of this paragraph.

paragraph.heading: Return of funds.—
paragraph.content: An entity that receives a subgrant from an eligible entity under subsection (f) and fails to comply with any requirement under this subsection shall return up to the entire amount of the subgrant to the eligible entity, at the discretion of the eligible entity or the Assistant Secretary.

subsection.heading: Regulations.—
subsection.content: The Assistant Secretary may issue such regulations or other guidance, forms, instructions, and publications as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the programs, projects, or activities authorized under this section, including to ensure that those programs, projects, or activities are completed in a timely and effective manner.

subparagraph.heading: Initial report.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after receiving grant funds under this section, for the sole purposes of providing transparency and providing information to inform future Federal broadband planning, an eligible entity shall submit to the Assistant Secretary a report that—

clause.content: describes the planned and actual use of funds;
describes the planned and actual process of subgranting;
identifies the establishment of appropriate mechanisms by the eligible entity to ensure that all subgrantees of the eligible entity comply with the eligible uses prescribed under subsection (f); and
includes any other information required by the Assistant Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Semiannual report.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after receiving grant funds under this section, and semiannually thereafter until the funds have been expended, an eligible entity shall submit to the Assistant Secretary a report, with respect to the 6-month period immediately preceding the report date, that—

clause.content: describes how the eligible entity expended the grant funds;
describes each service provided with the grant funds;
describes the number of locations at which broadband service was made available using the grant funds, and the number of those locations at which broadband service was utilized; and
certifies that the eligible entity complied with the requirements of this section and with any additional reporting requirements prescribed by the Assistant Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Final report.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after an eligible entity has expended all grant funds received under this section, the eligible entity shall submit to the Assistant Secretary a report that—

clause.content: describes how the eligible entity expended the funds;
describes each service provided with the grant funds;
describes the number of locations at which broadband service was made available using the grant funds, and the number of those locations at which broadband service was utilized;
includes each report that the eligible entity received from a subgrantee under paragraph (2); and
certifies that the eligible entity complied with the requirements of this section and with any additional reporting requirements prescribed by the Assistant Secretary.

subparagraph.heading:
Coordination.
Determination.Provision to fcc and usda.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to section 904(b)(2) of division FF of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (Public Law 116–260) (relating to an interagency agreement), the Assistant Secretary shall coordinate with the Commission and the Department of Agriculture, including providing the final reports received under subparagraph (C) to the Commission and the Department of Agriculture to be used when determining whether to award funds for the deployment of broadband under any program administered by those agencies.

clause.heading: Definitions.—
clause.content: In this subparagraph, the terms “agency” and “Federal broadband support program” have the meanings given those terms in section 903 of division FF of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (Public Law 116–260) (also known as the “ACCESS BROADBAND Act”).

clause.heading: Requirement.—
clause.content: An agency that offers a Federal broadband support program shall provide data to the Assistant Secretary, in a manner and format prescribed by the Assistant Secretary, to promote coordination of efforts to track construction and use of broadband infrastructure.

subparagraph.heading: Semiannual report.—
subparagraph.content: The recipient of a subgrant from an eligible entity under this section shall submit to the eligible entity a semiannual report for the duration 135 STAT. 1203 of the subgrant to track the effectiveness of the use of funds provided.

subparagraph.heading: Contents.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Each report submitted under subparagraph (A) shall—

clause.content: describe each type of project carried out using the subgrant and the duration of the subgrant;

clause.chapeau: in the case of a broadband infrastructure project—

subclause.content: List.include a list of addresses or locations that constitute the service locations that will be served by the broadband infrastructure to be constructed;
identify whether each address or location described in subclause (I) is residential, commercial, or a community anchor institution;
describe the types of facilities that have been constructed and installed;
describe the peak and off-peak actual speeds of the broadband service being offered;
describe the maximum advertised speed of the broadband service being offered;
describe the non-promotional prices, including any associated fees, charged for different tiers of broadband service being offered;

include any other data that would be required to comply with the data and mapping collection standards of the Commission under section 1.7004 of title 47, Code of Federal Regulations, or any successor regulation, for broadband infrastructure projects; and
comply with any other reasonable reporting requirements determined by the eligible entity or the Assistant Secretary; and

clause.content: Certification.certify that the information in the report is accurate.

paragraph.heading: Standardization and coordination.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Assistant Secretary and the Commission shall collaborate to—

subparagraph.content: standardize and coordinate reporting of locations at which broadband service was provided using grant funds received under this section in accordance with title VIII of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 641 et seq.); and
provide a standardized methodology to recipients of grants and subgrantees under this section for reporting the information described in subparagraph (A).

paragraph.heading: Information on broadband subsidies and low-income plans.—

subparagraph.heading: Establishment of website.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Assistant Secretary, in consultation with the Commission, shall establish a publicly available website that—

clause.chapeau: allows a consumer to determine, based on financial information entered by the consumer, whether the consumer is eligible—

subclause.content: to receive a Federal or State subsidy with respect to broadband service; or
for a low-income plan with respect to broadband service; and135 STAT. 1204

clause.content: contains information regarding how to apply for the applicable benefit described in clause (i).

subparagraph.heading: Provision of data.—
subparagraph.content: A Federal entity, State entity receiving Federal funds, or provider of broadband service that offers a subsidy or low-income plan, as applicable, with respect to broadband service shall provide data to the Assistant Secretary in a manner and format as established by the Assistant Secretary as necessary for the Assistant Secretary to carry out subparagraph (A).

subsection.heading: Relation to Other Public Funding.—
subsection.chapeau: Notwithstanding any other provision of law—

paragraph.content: an entity that has received amounts from the Federal Government or a State or local government for the purpose of expanding access to broadband service may receive a subgrant under subsection (f) in accordance with this section; and

the receipt of a subgrant under subsection (f) by an entity described in paragraph (1) of this subsection shall not affect the eligibility of the entity to receive the amounts from the Federal Government or a State or local government described in that paragraph.

subsection.heading: Supplement Not Supplant.—
subsection.content: Grant funds awarded to an eligible entity under this section shall be used to supplement, and not supplant, the amounts that the eligible entity would otherwise make available for the purposes for which the grant funds may be used.

subsection.heading: Sense of Congress Regarding Federal Agency Coordination.—
subsection.content: It is the sense of Congress that Federal agencies responsible for supporting broadband deployment, including the Commission, the Department of Commerce, and the Department of Agriculture, to the extent possible, should align the goals, application and reporting processes, and project requirements with respect to broadband deployment supported by those agencies.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The United States District Court for the District of Columbia shall have exclusive jurisdiction to review a decision of the Assistant Secretary made under this section.

paragraph.heading: Standard of review.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out any review described in paragraph (1), the court shall affirm the decision of the Assistant Secretary unless—

subparagraph.content: the decision was procured by corruption, fraud, or undue means;
there was actual partiality or corruption in the Assistant Secretary; or

subparagraph.chapeau: the Assistant Secretary was guilty of—

clause.content: misconduct in refusing to review the administrative record; or
any other misbehavior by which the rights of any party have been prejudiced.

subsection.heading: Exemption From Certain Laws.—
subsection.chapeau: Any action taken or decision made by the Assistant Secretary under this section shall be exempt from the requirements of—

paragraph.content: section 3506 of title 44, United States Code (commonly referred to as the “Paperwork Reduction Act”);
chapter 5 or 7 of title 5, United States Code (commonly referred to as the “Administrative Procedures Act”); and135 STAT. 1205
chapter 6 of title 5, United States Code (commonly referred to as the “Regulatory Flexibility Act”).

subsection.heading: Definition.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “Commission” means the Federal Communications Commission.

subsection.heading: Provision of Information.—
subsection.chapeau: A broadband provider shall provide the Commission with any information, in the format, type, or specification requested by the Commission, necessary to augment the collection of data by the Commission under—

paragraph.content: title VIII of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 641 et seq.); or
the Form 477 data collection program.

subsection.heading: Notice of Initial Broadband DATA Collection Filing Deadline.—
subsection.chapeau: The Commission—

paragraph.content: shall provide notice to broadband providers not later than 60 days before the initial deadline for submission of data under section 802(a)(1)(A) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 642(a)(1)(A)); and
notwithstanding any prior decision of the Commission to the contrary, shall not be required to provide notice not later than 6 months before the initial deadline described in paragraph (1).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Section 802(b)(1) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 802(b)(1)) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(D) Availability of census data.—The Secretary of Commerce shall submit to the Commission, for inclusion in the Fabric, a count of the aggregate number of housing units in each census block, as collected by the Bureau of the Census.” .

paragraph.heading: Provision of updated 2020 census data.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 30 days after receiving a request from the Commission, the Secretary of Commerce, in implementing the amendment made by paragraph (1), shall provide the Commission with a count of the aggregate number of housing units in each census block, as collected during the 2020 decennial census of population.

subsection.heading: Publication of Broadband DATA Maps on Internet.—
subsection.content: Section 802(c)(6) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 642(c)(6)) is amended, in the matter preceding paragraph (6), by inserting “, including on a publicly available website,” after “make public”.

section.heading: REPORT ON FUTURE OF UNIVERSAL SERVICE FUND.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section—

paragraph.content: the term “Commission” means the Federal Communications Commission; and

the term “universal service goals for broadband” means the statutorily mandated goals of universal service for advanced telecommunications capability under section 706 of the Telecommunications Act of 1996 (47 U.S.C. 1302).

subsection.heading: Evaluation.—
subsection.content: Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Commission shall commence a proceeding to evaluate the implications of this Act and the amendments made by this Act on how the Commission should achieve the universal service goals for broadband.135 STAT. 1206

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 270 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Commission shall submit to Congress a report on the options of the Commission for improving its effectiveness in achieving the universal service goals for broadband in light of this Act and the amendments made by this Act, and other legislation that addresses those goals.

paragraph.heading: Recommendations.—
paragraph.content: In the report submitted under paragraph (1), the Commission may make recommendations for Congress on further actions the Commission and Congress could take to improve the ability of the Commission to achieve the universal service goals for broadband.

paragraph.heading: Scope of universal service.—
paragraph.chapeau: In submitting the report under paragraph (1), the Commission—

subparagraph.content: may not in any way reduce the congressional mandate to achieve the universal service goals for broadband; and
may provide recommendations for Congress to expand the universal service goals for broadband, if the Commission believes such an expansion is in the public interest.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Broadband infrastructure.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “broadband infrastructure” means any cables, fiber optics, wiring, or other permanent (integral to the structure) infrastructure, including wireless infrastructure, that—

subparagraph.content: is capable of providing access to internet connections in individual locations; and
is an advanced telecommunications capability, as defined in section 706(d) of the Telecommunications Act of 1996 (47 U.S.C. 1302(d)).

paragraph.heading: Commission.—
paragraph.content: The term “Commission” means the Federal Communications Commission.

paragraph.heading: Deployment locations map.—
paragraph.content: The term “Deployment Locations Map” means the mapping tool required to be established under subsection (b).

subsection.heading:
Deadline.
Consultation.Establishment of Deployment Locations Map.—
subsection.content: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Commission shall, in consultation with all relevant Federal agencies, establish an online mapping tool to provide a locations overview of the overall geographic footprint of each broadband infrastructure deployment project funded by the Federal Government.

subsection.heading: Requirements.—
subsection.chapeau: The Deployment Locations Map shall be—

paragraph.content: the centralized, authoritative source of information on funding made available by the Federal Government for broadband infrastructure deployment in the United States; and
made publicly available on the website of the Commission.

subsection.heading: Functions.—
subsection.chapeau: In establishing the Deployment Locations Map, the Commission shall ensure that the Deployment Locations Map—

paragraph.chapeau: compiles data related to Federal funding for broadband infrastructure deployment provided by the Commission, the National Telecommunications and Information Administration, 135 STAT. 1207 the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of the Treasury, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Institute of Museum and Library Sciences, and any other Federal agency that provides such data relating to broadband infrastructure deployment funding to the Commission, including funding under—

subparagraph.content: this Act;
the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (Public Law 116–136);
the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (Public Law 116–260);
American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (Public Law 117–2); or
any Federal amounts appropriated or any Federal program authorized after the date of enactment of this Act to fund broadband infrastructure deployment;

paragraph.chapeau: contains data, with respect to each broadband infrastructure deployment program, relating to—

subparagraph.content: the Federal agency of jurisdiction;
the program title; and
the network type, including wired, terrestrial fixed, wireless, mobile, and satellite broadband infrastructure deployment;

paragraph.chapeau: allows users to manipulate the Deployment Locations Map to identify, search, and filter broadband infrastructure deployment projects by—

subparagraph.content: company name;
duration timeline, including the dates of a project’s beginning and ending, or anticipated beginning or ending date;
total number of locations to which a project makes service available; and
relevant download and upload speeds; and

paragraph.content: incorporates broadband service availability data as depicted in the Broadband Map created under section 802(c)(1) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 642(c)(1)).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Commission shall, in consultation with relevant Federal agencies, ensure the Deployment Locations Map is maintained and up to date on a periodic basis, but not less frequently than once every 180 days.

paragraph.heading: Reports.Other federal agencies.—
paragraph.content: Each Federal agency providing funding for broadband infrastructure deployment shall report relevant data to the Commission on a periodic basis.

subsection.heading: No Effect on Programmatic Missions.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to affect the programmatic missions of Federal agencies providing funding for broadband infrastructure development.

subsection.heading: Nonduplication.—
subsection.content: The requirements in this section shall be consistent with and avoid duplication with the provisions of section 903 of division FF of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (Public Law 116–260).

subsection.heading: Funding.—
subsection.content: Of the amounts appropriated to carry out this division under this Act, $10,000,000 shall be made available to carry out this section.135 STAT. 1208

section.heading: TRIBAL CONNECTIVITY TECHNICAL AMENDMENTS.
section.chapeau:
Section 905 of division N of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (Public Law 116–260)
47 USC 1305 note, 1705. is amended—

paragraph.chapeau: in subsection (c)—

subparagraph.content: in paragraph (1)(B), by striking “during the COVID–19 pandemic”;

subparagraph.chapeau: in paragraph (4)—

clause.chapeau: in subparagraph (A)—

Applicability.Multiple grant awards.—If the Assistant Secretary awards multiple grants to an eligible entity under this subsection, the deadlines under subparagraphs (A) and (B) shall apply individually to each grant award.” ; and
